agricultura.name: plow
agricultura.meaning: A walking plow with its handles and moldboard: plowing, tilling the field
agricultura.drawing: A walking plow with its handles and moldboard: plowing, tilling the field
agricultura.why: snowplow (vehiculos) is a truck's blade. The scope names the field plow. Draw the whole walking plow, not a part taken off a tractor.

agricultura.name: sowing
agricultura.meaning: A hand scattering seeds over a furrow: sowing, planting season
agricultura.drawing: A hand scattering seeds over a furrow: sowing, planting season
agricultura.why: seed-packet (plantas) is a garden packet, and germination is a sprouting seed. The scope names sowing in the field. The search hits are a packet and a calendar.

agricultura.name: cannabis
agricultura.meaning: A seven-leaflet cannabis leaf: hemp crops, CBD, dispensaries
agricultura.drawing: A seven-leaflet cannabis leaf: hemp crops, CBD, dispensaries
agricultura.why: weed is a garden-weed sprig, and Gota has no cannabis leaf. Lucide's cannabis has no equivalent. It isn't a religious or political symbol, but the judge may decide it stays out of the set.

agricultura.name: tractor-alert
agricultura.meaning: The tractor in profile with an alert badge. Used for a machine alert or fault code in farm fleet and telematics apps.
agricultura.drawing: The tractor in profile with an alert badge. Used for a machine alert or fault code in farm fleet and telematics apps.
agricultura.why: car-alert is a road car. Farm fleet and telematics platforms raise machine alerts and fault codes for each tractor. A vehicle is an object people manage, and in profile the badge doesn't hide the wheels and cab that identify it. The 'contains alert' conflict is just the badge family.

agricultura.name: farmland-plus
agricultura.meaning: Farmland from above with a plus badge. Used for adding a field or drawing its boundary in farm-management apps.
agricultura.drawing: Farmland from above with a plus badge. Used for adding a field or drawing its boundary in farm-management apps.
agricultura.why: farmland is the patchwork of fields from above (field map, parcels). Farm-management apps start every field record with 'add field' and drawing its boundary. A field is a place people manage. The 'contains plus' conflict is just the badge family. Agricultura's badges stay under 15%.

anatomia.name: skin-sunburn
anatomia.meaning: The skin block under sun rays: sunburn, UV damage
anatomia.drawing: The skin block under sun rays: sunburn, UV damage
anatomia.why: The skin family (rash, dry, oily, acne, wrinkles) has no UV damage.

anatomia.name: skin-burn
anatomia.meaning: The skin block with a flame: burn injury
anatomia.drawing: The skin block with a flame: burn injury
anatomia.why: Rash is irritation. A burn is a thermal injury and has no icon.

anatomia.name: body-side
anatomia.meaning: The body outline in profile: side view for posture, symptom pickers and measurements
anatomia.drawing: The body outline in profile: side view for posture, symptom pickers and measurements
anatomia.why: body and body-back are the front and back views. The profile completes them. The search hit on head-side is only the word 'side'.

animales.name: pangolin
animales.meaning: A pangolin in profile, covered in overlapping scales, with a long tapering tail. Used for trafficked and endangered species.
animales.drawing: A pangolin in profile, covered in overlapping scales, with a long tapering tail. Used for trafficked and endangered species.
animales.why: The armadillo is rigid bands. The pangolin is overlapping scales and a long tail, and it's the conservation icon people look for.

animales.name: capybara
animales.meaning: A capybara sitting: a large blocky rodent with a square snout and no tail. Used for wildlife, wetlands, and as a popular mascot.
animales.drawing: A capybara sitting: a large blocky rodent with a square snout and no tail. Used for wildlife, wetlands, and as a popular mascot.
animales.why: field-mouse is small and long-tailed. The capybara is big, tailless, and square-headed.

animales.name: water-buffalo
animales.meaning: A water buffalo with wide horns sweeping back from its head. Used for Asian farming, rice paddies, and buffalo dairy.
animales.drawing: A water buffalo with wide horns sweeping back from its head. Used for Asian farming, rice paddies, and buffalo dairy.
animales.why: The bison has the shoulder hump and short horns. The water buffalo has no hump and wide backswept horns.

animales.name: bighorn-sheep
animales.meaning: A bighorn sheep, a ram with heavy horns curled around its ears. Used for mountain wildlife and for rams on the farm.
animales.drawing: A bighorn sheep, a ram with heavy horns curled around its ears. Used for mountain wildlife and for rams on the farm.
animales.why: sheep is woolly and has no horns, and goat has short swept horns and a beard. This name avoids 'ram', which the search ties to memory (RAM).

animales.name: badger
animales.meaning: A badger low to the ground with its black-and-white striped face. Used for woodland wildlife.
animales.drawing: A badger low to the ground with its black-and-white striped face. Used for woodland wildlife.
animales.why: The raccoon has an eye mask and a ringed tail, and the skunk a plume tail. The badger is low and long with a striped face. The search hit on shaving-brush is only its 'badger brush' keyword.

animales.name: sabertooth
animales.meaning: A saber-toothed cat with two long fangs. Used for the Ice Age and prehistoric mammals.
animales.drawing: A saber-toothed cat with two long fangs. Used for the Ice Age and prehistoric mammals.
animales.why: It's the mammoth's prehistoric partner. Its fangs are its trait, and tiger has none.

animales.name: pegasus
animales.meaning: A winged horse in flight. Used for fantasy, mythology, and kids' apps.
animales.drawing: A winged horse in flight. Used for fantasy, mythology, and kids' apps.
animales.why: The unicorn has a horn and Pegasus has wings: another creature, beside the unicorn the set already draws.

animales.name: horse-face
animales.meaning: A horse's face from the front, with its ears and forelock. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A horse's face from the front, with its ears and forelock. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: horse is the profile, and unicorn-face carries the horn. This is the plain horse face of the face family (bear-face, cow-face, pig-face).

animales.name: goat-face
animales.meaning: A goat's face with short horns and a beard. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A goat's face with short horns and a beard. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: goat is the full body. The beard and horns tell it apart from sheep-face.

animales.name: deer-face
animales.meaning: A deer's face from the front with branching antlers. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A deer's face from the front with branching antlers. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: Those are full bodies in profile. The face family has no deer.

animales.name: giraffe-face
animales.meaning: A giraffe's long face with its two ossicones and ears. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A giraffe's long face with its two ossicones and ears. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: giraffe is the full body. The ossicones make the face read on its own.

animales.name: zebra-face
animales.meaning: A zebra's face with its striped muzzle and upright mane. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A zebra's face with its striped muzzle and upright mane. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: zebra is the full body. The stripes are drawn as shape, not print.

animales.name: hippo-face
animales.meaning: A hippo's face with its wide muzzle, nostrils, and small ears. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A hippo's face with its wide muzzle, nostrils, and small ears. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: hippo is the full body. The face family has no hippo.

animales.name: raccoon-face
animales.meaning: A raccoon's face with its dark eye mask and pointed ears. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A raccoon's face with its dark eye mask and pointed ears. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: raccoon is the full body. The mask makes the face the recognizable part.

animales.name: mouse-face
animales.meaning: A mouse's face with big round ears and whiskers. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A mouse's face with big round ears and whiskers. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: field-mouse is the full body, and plain 'mouse' is the device in dispositivos. The -face suffix keeps it in the animal family.

animales.name: rabbit-face
animales.meaning: A rabbit's face with two long upright ears. Used for avatars, stickers, emoji, and Easter.
animales.drawing: A rabbit's face with two long upright ears. Used for avatars, stickers, emoji, and Easter.
animales.why: rabbit is the pet's full body. The face family has no rabbit, and it's one of the most used animal emoji.

animales.name: rhino-face
animales.meaning: A rhino's face from the front with its horn. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A rhino's face from the front with its horn. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: rhino is the full body in profile.

animales.name: moose-face
animales.meaning: A moose's face with broad palmate antlers and a drooping muzzle. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A moose's face with broad palmate antlers and a drooping muzzle. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: moose is the full body. Its palmate antlers tell it apart from deer-face's branching ones.

animales.name: boar-face
animales.meaning: A wild boar's face with tusks curving up from its snout. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A wild boar's face with tusks curving up from its snout. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: pig-face has no tusks, and boar is the full body.

animales.name: gorilla-face
animales.meaning: A gorilla's face with its heavy brow ridge and flat nose. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.drawing: A gorilla's face with its heavy brow ridge and flat nose. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
animales.why: monkey-face has big side ears and a pale muzzle. The gorilla is told by its brow and crest. Round 11 dropped the gorilla's body (it read as a stone), not its face.

archivos.name: folder-zip
archivos.why: file-zip is a compressed file. The zipped folder is how most systems show an archive.

arte.name: swatch-book
arte.meaning: A fan deck of color swatch cards pinned at one end; paint colors, color guides.
arte.drawing: A fan deck of color swatch cards pinned at one end; paint colors, color guides.
arte.why: fabric-swatch (ropa) is textile samples, and color-swatches (controles) is four dots. The fan deck of paint cards is in scope. Heroicons' swatch maps here too.

arte.name: drawing-mannequin
arte.meaning: An artist's wooden jointed figure on its stand; figure drawing, poses.
arte.drawing: An artist's wooden jointed figure on its stand; figure drawing, poses.
arte.why: mannequin (comercio) is a dress form. The jointed wooden figure is an artist's tool.

arte.name: embroidery-hoop
arte.meaning: An embroidery hoop with its screw clamp, a stitched motif and a needle; embroidery, cross-stitch.
arte.drawing: An embroidery hoop with its screw clamp, a stitched motif and a needle; embroidery, cross-stitch.
arte.why: The scope names embroidery, and nothing draws it. The clamp at the top keeps the hoop from reading as a ring.

arte.name: marker-pen
arte.meaning: A felt-tip marker with its bullet tip and cap; markers, drawing, coloring.
arte.drawing: A felt-tip marker with its bullet tip and cap; markers, drawing, coloring.
arte.why: The scope names markers, and the highlighter (edicion) has a wedge tip. Risk: the two can merge at 18 px, so the bullet tip and the cap have to carry it.

aves-insectos.name: cockatoo
aves-insectos.meaning: A cockatoo with its raised crest. Used for pet birds and tropical birds.
aves-insectos.drawing: A cockatoo with its raised crest. Used for pet birds and tropical birds.
aves-insectos.why: parrot (a macaw) has no crest, and the crest is what tells a cockatoo.

aves-insectos.name: quail
aves-insectos.meaning: A plump quail with a teardrop plume on its head. Used for game birds and quail eggs.
aves-insectos.drawing: A plump quail with a teardrop plume on its head. Used for game birds and quail eggs.
aves-insectos.why: Neither has the plume, which is what tells a quail at small sizes.

aves-insectos.name: bird-search
aves-insectos.meaning: A bird with a magnifier badge. Used to identify a bird, as in bird ID apps.
aves-insectos.drawing: A bird with a magnifier badge. Used to identify a bird, as in bird ID apps.
aves-insectos.why: bird-plus means logging a sighting. This means identifying a species, as fish-search does in mar and paw-search in mascotas. names.mjs flags 'contains search', which is the badge.

aves-insectos.name: frog-face
aves-insectos.meaning: A frog's face with bulging eyes on top and a wide mouth. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
aves-insectos.drawing: A frog's face with bulging eyes on top and a wide mouth. Used for avatars, stickers, and emoji.
aves-insectos.why: frog is the full body. The frog face is one of the most used animal emoji, and it joins animales's face family.

aves-insectos.name: ankylosaurus
aves-insectos.meaning: An ankylosaurus with its armored back and club tail. Used for dinosaurs and kids' apps.
aves-insectos.drawing: An ankylosaurus with its armored back and club tail. Used for dinosaurs and kids' apps.
aves-insectos.why: The stegosaurus has back plates and tail spikes. The ankylosaurus is low armor with a club at the tail.

aviacion.name: biplane
aviacion.meaning: A biplane in profile with two stacked wings: vintage aircraft, scenic flights, air shows
aviacion.drawing: A biplane in profile with two stacked wings: vintage aircraft, scenic flights, air shows
aviacion.why: The stacked wings make a kind of its own among planes by kind.

aviacion.name: hang-glider
aviacion.meaning: A delta-wing hang glider with its pilot hanging below: hang gliding
aviacion.drawing: A delta-wing hang glider with its pilot hanging below: hang gliding
aviacion.why: glider is the sailplane, so the name shares a word but not a base. A hang glider is a triangle wing with a pilot under it.

aviacion.name: paraglider
aviacion.meaning: A paraglider's wide arched wing with lines down to the pilot: paragliding flights
aviacion.drawing: A paraglider's wide arched wing with lines down to the pilot: paragliding flights
aviacion.why: parachute (deportes) is a round canopy for falling, and a paraglider is a wing for flying. Material has paragliding. Risk: keep the arc wide and flat so it doesn't read as the parachute. It could also live in deportes.

aviacion.name: plane-plus
aviacion.meaning: A plane with a plus badge: add a flight to a trip
aviacion.drawing: A plane with a plus badge: add a flight to a trip
aviacion.why: plane has check, x, clock, alert, search, and wifi but no plus. Trip planners need 'add flight'.

aviacion.name: helipad
aviacion.meaning: A circle with an H: a helipad or heliport, on maps and on hospitals and buildings.
aviacion.drawing: A circle with an H: a helipad or heliport, on maps and on hospitals and buildings.
aviacion.why: helicopter is the aircraft. The pad is a place, as runway is to the plane. Its H is a single letter and is the symbol itself, like parking's P. helicopter and windsock only carry 'helipad' as a tag.

belleza.name: hair-clip
belleza.meaning: Claw clip with interlocking teeth: hair claw, barrette
belleza.drawing: Claw clip with interlocking teeth: hair claw, barrette
belleza.why: A pin and a claw clip are different accessories. hair-extensions is the hair itself.

belleza.name: waxing
belleza.meaning: Wax warmer pot with a spatula: waxing, hair removal
belleza.drawing: Wax warmer pot with a spatula: waxing, hair removal
belleza.why: There is no hair removal by wax. The search hits on the moon phases are only the word.

belleza.name: ear-piercing
belleza.meaning: The ear with a stud and a hoop: piercing studio, ear piercing
belleza.drawing: The ear with a stud and a hoop: piercing studio, ear piercing
belleza.why: earrings (ropa) is the jewelry. The ear with a stud is the piercing service, drawn on anatomia's ear.

belleza.name: toothbrush-sparkles
belleza.meaning: Toothbrush with sparkles: teeth brushed, oral hygiene done, fresh breath
belleza.drawing: Toothbrush with sparkles: teeth brushed, oral hygiene done, fresh breath
belleza.why: The brush alone is the object. The sparkles mean 'clean', as in hand-sparkles; the 'sparkle' contains is that family mark.

belleza.name: hair-bun
belleza.meaning: Hair gathered into a bun on top: updo, bun
belleza.drawing: Hair gathered into a bun on top: updo, bun
belleza.why: It is a different hairstyle in the same family. bobby-pin and scrunchie are only accessories.

belleza.name: hair-ponytail
belleza.meaning: Hair tied back into a ponytail
belleza.drawing: Hair tied back into a ponytail
belleza.why: It is a different style. scrunchie is the tie alone.

bienes-raices.name: property-tax
bienes-raices.meaning: Property tax: a house with a percent sign on its front, the yearly tax on a property (predial)
bienes-raices.drawing: Property tax: a house with a percent sign on its front, the yearly tax on a property (predial)
bienes-raices.why: house-price is what the home costs and condo-fee is the HOA fee; property tax is a recurring cost on its own in listings and property management

bienes-raices.name: lease-check
bienes-raices.meaning: Signed lease: the lease with a check badge. A rental agreement signed by both parties and now in force, a status in property-management and rental apps.
bienes-raices.drawing: Signed lease: the lease with a check badge. A rental agreement signed by both parties and now in force, a status in property-management and rental apps.
bienes-raices.why: lease-application is the tenant's application (edit badge), lease-renewal is a renewal (sync) and lease-expiring is the end date (clock). The lease family lacks its signed state. contract-signed is a generic contract in comercio, not the lease's gabled page.

bienestar.name: plate-balanced
bienestar.meaning: A plate split into portions (half and two quarters): balanced diet, healthy plate
bienestar.drawing: A plate split into portions (half and two quarters): balanced diet, healthy plate
bienestar.why: cocina's plates only log meals. The scope's nutrition plate is the portioned plate, and it is missing.

bienestar.name: yoga-triangle
bienestar.meaning: Triangle pose: legs wide, torso tilted, one arm down to the shin and one up
bienestar.drawing: Triangle pose: legs wide, torso tilted, one arm down to the shin and one up
bienestar.why: It is a different standing pose. Standing poses read, and floor poses were dropped. formas' 'triangle' is only the pose's name.

bienestar.name: yoga-dancer
bienestar.meaning: Dancer pose: standing on one leg, the back foot held up behind, the other arm reaching forward
bienestar.drawing: Dancer pose: standing on one leg, the back foot held up behind, the other arm reaching forward
bienestar.why: Tree rests the foot on the thigh. Dancer holds the back foot up behind.

bienestar.name: acupuncture
bienestar.meaning: Needles set in the skin block: acupuncture, dry needling
bienestar.drawing: Needles set in the skin block: acupuncture, dry needling
bienestar.why: No needle therapy exists. It is drawn on anatomia's skin block.

bienestar.name: mind-cloud
bienestar.meaning: The head with a cloud inside: brain fog, low mood, depression
bienestar.drawing: The head with a cloud inside: brain fog, low mood, depression
bienestar.why: Tangled means anxiety. The cloud means brain fog or low mood. The mind-* family explains the contains.

bienestar.name: mind-sprout
bienestar.meaning: The head with a sprout inside: personal growth, growth mindset
bienestar.drawing: The head with a sprout inside: personal growth, growth mindset
bienestar.why: hand-sprout means nurturing something else. A sprout in the head means personal growth. The mind-* family explains the name.

bienestar.name: breath-hold
bienestar.meaning: The breath with a pause between in and out: hold your breath, breathing exercise step
bienestar.drawing: The breath with a pause between in and out: hold your breath, breathing exercise step
bienestar.why: box-breathing is the whole pattern. breath-in and breath-out are drawn as phases, and hold is the missing phase.

calendario.name: calendar-sort
calendario.meaning: Sort by date: order items by their date
calendario.drawing: Sort by date: order items by their date
calendario.why: sort orders by any key. Sorting by date is the sort lists offer most.

calendario.name: clock-sort
calendario.meaning: Sort by time: order items by their time (most recent first)
calendario.drawing: Sort by time: order items by their time (most recent first)
calendario.why: The same reason as calendar-sort, with time as the key.

calendario.name: stopwatch-reset
calendario.meaning: Reset timer: set the stopwatch back to zero
calendario.drawing: Reset timer: set the stopwatch back to zero
calendario.why: play, pause, and stop exist. Reset is the fourth stopwatch control.

calendario.name: alarm-minus
calendario.why: alarm-off silences an alarm. alarm-minus removes it and pairs with alarm-plus.

calendario.name: alarm-ringing
calendario.meaning: Alarm going off: an alarm clock ringing now
calendario.drawing: Alarm going off: an alarm clock ringing now
calendario.why: alarm-clock is set or idle and rings only in its animation. The ringing state needs a still icon, as bell has bell-ringing.

calendario.name: calendar-poll
calendario.meaning: Scheduling poll: invitees vote on times to find a meeting slot
calendario.drawing: Scheduling poll: invitees vote on times to find a meeting slot
calendario.why: calendar-sparkle schedules automatically, while the poll asks the invitees.

calendario.name: calendar-weekend
calendario.meaning: Weekend: the days off at the end of the week
calendario.drawing: Weekend: the days off at the end of the week
calendario.why: calendar-workday marks business days. The weekend is its counterpart in work-week settings.

calendario.name: shift-open
calendario.meaning: Open shift: an unassigned shift anyone can pick up
calendario.drawing: Open shift: an unassigned shift anyone can pick up
calendario.why: shift-swap trades a shift between two people. An open shift has no one assigned yet.

camping.name: campfire-cooking
camping.meaning: A pot hanging from a tripod over a campfire: cooking outdoors
camping.drawing: A pot hanging from a tripod over a campfire: cooking outdoors
camping.why: camp-stove is the gas burner and campfire is the fire alone. Cooking over an open fire is its own outdoor activity. 'contains cooking' is the kitchen word in cocina.

camping.name: map-pin-fish
camping.meaning: A map pin with a fish: a fishing spot on the map
camping.drawing: A map pin with a fish: a fishing spot on the map
camping.why: The map-pin family has campsite, bird sighting, and pet-friendly pins but no fishing spot, which fishing apps rely on.

camping.name: tipi
camping.meaning: A tall cone tent with its poles crossed above the top and a door flap: tipi stays and glamping.
camping.drawing: A tall cone tent with its poles crossed above the top and a door flap: tipi stays and glamping.
camping.why: The bell tent has low walls and a single pole. The tipi is a pure cone with its poles sticking out the top. Campsite booking lists it as its own accommodation type, next to the yurt, treehouse and cabin that Gota already draws.

ciberseguridad.name: qr-phishing
ciberseguridad.meaning: A QR code with the phishing hook: quishing, a malicious QR code that leads to a fake site.
ciberseguridad.drawing: A QR code with the phishing hook: quishing, a malicious QR code that leads to a fake site.
ciberseguridad.why: The phishing family splits by channel (smishing, vishing, spear-phishing). QR-code phishing on parking meters, mail, and menus is a channel it lacks.

ciberseguridad.name: sim-swap
ciberseguridad.meaning: A SIM card with swap arrows: SIM swap fraud, where a phone number is ported to an attacker's SIM to take over its codes.
ciberseguridad.drawing: A SIM card with swap arrows: SIM swap fraud, where a phone number is ported to an attacker's SIM to take over its codes.
ciberseguridad.why: sim-card is the plain card, and compromised-account is the generic outcome. SIM swapping is a named attack with its own warnings in banking and carrier apps.

ciberseguridad.name: bot-detection
ciberseguridad.meaning: A robot head under a magnifier: bot detection and management, telling automated traffic from humans.
ciberseguridad.drawing: A robot head under a magnifier: bot detection and management, telling automated traffic from humans.
ciberseguridad.why: captcha (controles) is the challenge shown to a person, and botnet is the infected network. ai-detection is AI-generated content. The defense that scores traffic as bot or human has no icon.

ciberseguridad.name: key-pair
ciberseguridad.meaning: Two keys side by side, one public and one private: public-key cryptography, asymmetric keys, PKI.
ciberseguridad.drawing: Two keys side by side, one public and one private: public-key cryptography, asymmetric keys, PKI.
ciberseguridad.why: key-crypto (comercio) is a single wallet key, and encryption and digital-signature show what the pair does, not the pair. Asymmetric keys are the base of certificates, SSH, and signing.

ciberseguridad.name: security-key-plus
ciberseguridad.meaning: Hardware security key with a plus: register a security key in an account's sign-in settings
ciberseguridad.drawing: Hardware security key with a plus: register a security key in an account's sign-in settings
ciberseguridad.why: key-plus is a generic key or passkey credential. security-key is the physical FIDO token, and «Add security key» is a separate entry in Google, Microsoft and GitHub account security. ciberseguridad has no badges yet.

ciencia.name: centrifuge
ciencia.meaning: A benchtop lab centrifuge with its lid raised and tubes slanted in the rotor: spinning samples down, separation
ciencia.drawing: A benchtop lab centrifuge with its lid raised and tubes slanted in the rotor: spinning samples down, separation
ciencia.why: microtube is the tube a centrifuge spins. Nothing draws the machine itself, and the scope names it. Draw it by the slanted tubes around the hub so it doesn't read as a box.

ciencia.name: bacteria
ciencia.meaning: A rod-shaped bacterium with pili and a curling flagellum: microbiology, germs, cultures
ciencia.drawing: A rod-shaped bacterium with pili and a curling flagellum: microbiology, germs, cultures
ciencia.why: petri-dish is the culture dish and virus (salud) is a spiked sphere. Nothing draws the bacterium itself, and the scope names it.

ciencia.name: flask-retort
ciencia.meaning: The retort, a round glass vessel whose long neck bends down to one side: distillation, classic chemistry
ciencia.drawing: The retort, a round glass vessel whose long neck bends down to one side: distillation, classic chemistry
ciencia.why: flask-round has a straight upright neck. The retort's neck bends sideways into a downspout. The name puts it in the flask family (flask-round, flask-volumetric); a bare 'retort' would clash with lab-stand's 'retort stand' keyword.

ciencia.name: lever
ciencia.meaning: A bar on a triangular fulcrum lifting a block, with an arrow pressing the long end: simple machines, mechanical advantage
ciencia.drawing: A bar on a triangular fulcrum lifting a block, with an arrow pressing the long end: simple machines, mechanical advantage
ciencia.why: inclined-plane is the other simple machine, and seesaw (lugares) is a playground ride with seats and handles. The lever is the bare bar, fulcrum, load and effort arrow. Check it against the seesaw.

ciencia.name: gravity
ciencia.meaning: An apple falling toward a ground line with a downward arrow: gravity, free fall, weight
ciencia.drawing: An apple falling toward a ground line with a downward arrow: gravity, free fall, weight
ciencia.why: force is an arrow pushing a box, and orbit/trajectory are paths around a planet. Nothing shows gravity itself, and the scope names it.

ciencia.name: flask-plus
ciencia.meaning: Flask with a plus badge: new experiment, add an experiment
ciencia.drawing: Flask with a plus badge: new experiment, add an experiment
ciencia.why: flask-check is a successful experiment. This is the action that starts a new one in lab notebooks and LIMS.

ciencia.name: flask-x
ciencia.meaning: Flask with an x badge: failed experiment
ciencia.drawing: Flask with an x badge: failed experiment
ciencia.why: The failed state that pairs with flask-check, as test-tube-x pairs with test-tube-check.

ciencia.name: flask-clock
ciencia.meaning: Flask with a clock badge: experiment in progress, incubation time
ciencia.drawing: Flask with a clock badge: experiment in progress, incubation time
ciencia.why: The running or incubating state between a new experiment and a finished one.

ciencia.name: test-tube-clock
ciencia.meaning: Test tube with a clock badge: sample pending, lab results pending
ciencia.drawing: Test tube with a clock badge: sample pending, lab results pending
ciencia.why: test-tube-check and test-tube-x are approved and rejected samples. Pending results, the third state that lab and patient portals show, has no icon.

ciencia.name: dna-search
ciencia.meaning: DNA helix with a search badge: genetic test, genome analysis, ancestry
ciencia.drawing: DNA helix with a search badge: genetic test, genome analysis, ancestry
ciencia.why: dna is the helix and gene-editing cuts it. Nothing shows genetic testing or genome analysis, which health and ancestry apps need.

ciencia.name: research-paper-check
ciencia.meaning: Research paper with a check badge: peer-reviewed, accepted for publication
ciencia.drawing: Research paper with a check badge: peer-reviewed, accepted for publication
ciencia.why: research-paper-search is a literature search. This is the accepted, peer-reviewed paper.

ciencia.name: research-paper-plus
ciencia.meaning: Research paper with a plus badge. Used for adding a paper to a reference library or submitting a manuscript.
ciencia.drawing: Research paper with a plus badge. Used for adding a paper to a reference library or submitting a manuscript.
ciencia.why: research-paper-search is a literature search and research-paper-check (first pass) is a paper accepted after peer review. Reference managers and journal submission portals have adding or submitting a paper as their main action. The 'contains plus' conflict is just the badge family. Ciencia's badges go from 10 to 11 out of about 91.

clima.name: sun-snowflake
clima.meaning: A sun and a snowflake split by a diagonal. Used for hot and cold, all-season, and the weather's heat-or-cold range.
clima.drawing: A sun and a snowflake split by a diagonal. Used for hot and cold, all-season, and the weather's heat-or-cold range.
clima.why: heat-cool is a flame and a snowflake for the HVAC mode. cloud-sun-snow is snow showers. This is the weather and season sense Lucide's sun-snow and SF's sun.snow carry.

clima.name: wind-arrow-up
clima.meaning: Wind lines with an up arrow. Used for wind picking up, or stronger wind ahead.
clima.drawing: Wind lines with an up arrow. Used for wind picking up, or stronger wind ahead.
clima.why: wind is the condition, and wind-alert is the advisory. This is the trend, as barometer-arrow-up is for pressure. The arrow is a family modifier, so 'contains arrow-up' holds.

clima.name: wind-arrow-down
clima.meaning: Wind lines with a down arrow. Used for wind easing, or calmer wind ahead.
clima.drawing: Wind lines with a down arrow. Used for wind easing, or calmer wind ahead.
clima.why: It's the falling trend that pairs with wind-arrow-up, as barometer-arrow-down does.

clima.name: umbrella-percent
clima.meaning: An umbrella with a percent sign. Used for the chance of rain, or probability of precipitation.
clima.drawing: An umbrella with a percent sign. Used for the chance of rain, or probability of precipitation.
clima.why: The scope names the chance of rain. droplet-percent is relative humidity. It follows that same percent pattern.

clima.name: cloud-percent
clima.meaning: A cloud with a percent sign. Used for cloud cover.
clima.drawing: A cloud with a percent sign. Used for cloud cover.
clima.why: clouds is the 'cloudy' condition. Cloud cover is a metric weather apps list beside humidity and the chance of rain.

clima.name: thermometer-droplet
clima.meaning: A thermometer with a droplet. Used for the dew point reading.
clima.drawing: A thermometer with a droplet. Used for the dew point reading.
clima.why: dew is droplets on grass, the condition, and it carries 'dew point' only as a keyword. The dew point is a temperature, and Material and SF (drop.degreesign) draw it as its own icon.

clima.name: thermometer-moon
clima.meaning: A thermometer with a moon. Used for the overnight low, or night temperature.
clima.drawing: A thermometer with a moon. Used for the overnight low, or night temperature.
clima.why: thermometer-sun is the daytime high. This is its night pair, and the thermometer family's modifier.

clima.name: moon-haze
clima.meaning: A moon behind haze lines. Used for a hazy night.
clima.drawing: A moon behind haze lines. Used for a hazy night.
clima.why: It's the night pair of sun-haze, the way the set pairs every cloud-sun-* with a cloud-moon-*.

clima.name: occluded-front
clima.meaning: A front line with alternating triangles and semicircles on one side. Used for an occluded front on a weather map.
clima.drawing: A front line with alternating triangles and semicircles on one side. Used for an occluded front on a weather map.
clima.why: Those are the other two map symbols. The occluded front is the third of the four standard front symbols.

clima.name: stationary-front
clima.meaning: A front line with triangles on one side and semicircles on the other. Used for a stationary front on a weather map.
clima.drawing: A front line with triangles on one side and semicircles on the other. Used for a stationary front on a weather map.
clima.why: It's the fourth standard front symbol. Its marks on opposite sides are what tell it apart.

clima.name: cloud-rainbow
clima.meaning: A rainbow arching out from behind a cloud. Used for clearing after rain, or a rainbow in the forecast.
clima.drawing: A rainbow arching out from behind a cloud. Used for clearing after rain, or a rainbow in the forecast.
clima.why: rainbow is three bands alone (tagged pride and hope). SF's cloud.rainbow.half and Phosphor's rainbow-cloud are the weather version.

comercio.name: card-minus
comercio.meaning: Remove card: the card with a minus badge, unlink a payment method
comercio.drawing: Remove card: the card with a minus badge, unlink a payment method
comercio.why: add card exists, remove doesn't; card-declined is a failed payment

comercio.name: hand-coins
comercio.meaning: Money received: an open hand holding coins, for a payment received, wages, an allowance or a loan
comercio.drawing: Money received: an open hand holding coins, for a payment received, wages, an allowance or a loan
comercio.why: cash-in is a deposit into an account and donation is giving (hand with heart); the receiving hand is a separate, very common drawing

comercio.name: banknote-check
comercio.meaning: Paid in cash: the banknote with a check badge, cash payment received
comercio.drawing: Paid in cash: the banknote with a check badge, cash payment received
comercio.why: invoice-paid and bill-presenter-check are paid documents; this marks a cash payment taken at the till

comercio.name: bag-question
comercio.meaning: Order help: the shopping bag with a question badge, a question about an order
comercio.drawing: Order help: the shopping bag with a question badge, a question about an order
comercio.why: help is generic; shops put order help next to returns (bag-return) and exchanges (bag-exchange). It also covers SF cart.badge.questionmark.

comercio.name: receipt-x
comercio.meaning: Voided transaction: the receipt with an x badge. Marks a sale or charge cancelled after it was recorded, in a POS order list, a bank's activity, or an expense app's rejected receipts.
comercio.drawing: Voided transaction: the receipt with an x badge. Marks a sale or charge cancelled after it was recorded, in a POS order list, a bank's activity, or an expense app's rejected receipts.
comercio.why: bag-remove is the shopper cancelling a purchase in the shop's flow. receipt-x marks the recorded transaction itself as void. The receipt family has receipt-clock, receipt-scan and receipt-tax but no cancelled state.

comercio.name: price-tag-arrow-up
comercio.meaning: Price increase: the price tag with an up arrow badge, for a product's price history and repricing alerts.
comercio.drawing: Price increase: the price tag with an up arrow badge, for a product's price history and repricing alerts.
comercio.why: price-tag-arrow-down is a price drop and house-price-up is a property's value. Nothing shows a product's price going up. It completes the pair the same way house-price-up/-down already do.

comercio.name: invoice-x
comercio.meaning: Voided invoice: the invoice with an x badge. An issued invoice cancelled so it can no longer be paid (the 'void' status in Stripe, QuickBooks and Xero).
comercio.drawing: Voided invoice: the invoice with an x badge. An issued invoice cancelled so it can no longer be paid (the 'void' status in Stripe, QuickBooks and Xero).
comercio.why: invoice-minus is a credit note, which offsets an invoice that stays valid. invoice-due is unpaid and invoice-paid is settled. Nothing says the invoice was cancelled. The family is already built for badges (plus, check, clock, minus).

comercio.name: bank-check
comercio.meaning: Verified bank account: the bank with a check badge. A linked account that has been confirmed for payouts or direct debits, for example after micro-deposits.
comercio.drawing: Verified bank account: the bank with a check badge. A linked account that has been confirmed for payouts or direct debits, for example after micro-deposits.
comercio.why: bank-plus is the action of linking an account. account-statement-check is a reconciled statement (books match), not a verified account. The search hit cheque is a paper check, which is a different object.

comercio.name: budget-alert
comercio.meaning: Over budget: the budget gauge with an alert badge. A category or project that has spent past its limit, as in budgeting and spend-management apps.
comercio.drawing: Over budget: the budget gauge with an alert badge. A category or project that has spent past its limit, as in budgeting and spend-management apps.
comercio.why: budget shows how much of a limit is spent as a value on its ring. It has no state for going over the limit. revenue-down and money-wings are income falling and spending in general, not an exceeded limit.

comida.name: tamale
comida.meaning: A tamale in its corn husk, folded open at one end over the masa: Mexican and Latin American food, tamalerías
comida.drawing: A tamale in its corn husk, folded open at one end over the masa: Mexican and Latin American food, tamalerías
comida.why: The burrito is a soft tortilla roll. A tamale is masa in a corn husk, told by the husk's ridges and its folded, tied ends. It is the one common Unicode food emoji (🫔) Gota doesn't draw yet, and a staple in Mexico.

comida.name: fortune-cookie
comida.meaning: A folded fortune cookie with its paper slip poking out: Chinese-American restaurants, a dessert, a daily fortune or tip
comida.drawing: A folded fortune cookie with its paper slip poking out: Chinese-American restaurants, a dessert, a daily fortune or tip
comida.why: cookie is a flat round biscuit with chips that stands for browser cookies. The fortune cookie is a folded crescent with a slip, a different object (🥠). 'Contains cookie' is just its plain English name, not a family.

comida.name: fondue
comida.meaning: A fondue pot over its small burner with two long forks dipping in: cheese or chocolate fondue, a shared dinner
comida.drawing: A fondue pot over its small burner with two long forks dipping in: cheese or chocolate fondue, a shared dinner
comida.why: The cooking pot is a stockpot on its own. Fondue is the round pot on a stand with a flame under it and long forks dipping in (🫕). The search hit (cloud-sleet) is unrelated.

comida.name: spring-roll
comida.meaning: A fried spring roll cut on the bias to show its filling: egg rolls, lumpia, Chinese, Vietnamese, and Thai starters
comida.drawing: A fried spring roll cut on the bias to show its filling: egg rolls, lumpia, Chinese, Vietnamese, and Thai starters
comida.why: The burrito is a thick soft wrap. A spring roll is a thin crisp cylinder, and no icon draws it. Risk: on its own it can read as a log, so the bias cut with the filling has to carry it.

comida.name: corn-dog
comida.meaning: A battered sausage on a stick: fair food, American and Korean street snacks
comida.drawing: A battered sausage on a stick: fair food, American and Korean street snacks
comida.why: The hot dog sits in a split bun, and ice-pop is a flat bar. The corn dog is a tapered batter shell on a stick. 'Contains dog' is the food's name and has nothing to do with mascotas.

comida.name: paella
comida.meaning: A wide, shallow paella pan with two loop handles, holding rice, a shrimp, and a lemon wedge: Spanish food, rice dishes to share
comida.drawing: A wide, shallow paella pan with two loop handles, holding rice, a shrimp, and a lemon wedge: Spanish food, rice dishes to share
comida.why: The frying pan has one long handle and is empty. The paella pan is shallow with two loop handles and the dish on it (🥘 'shallow pan of food'). The mussel hit is the shellfish, which only lists paella as a keyword.

comida.name: candy-apple
comida.meaning: An apple dipped in caramel or candy, on a stick: fair food, Halloween, manzana con chamoy
comida.drawing: An apple dipped in caramel or candy, on a stick: fair food, Halloween, manzana con chamoy
comida.why: apple is the fruit. The stick and the dripped coating make it a sweet. It's named the way people search for it. If it's drawn on the apple's base, the judge may prefer apple-candy, but that name reads as apple-flavored candy.

comida.name: gelatin
comida.meaning: A fluted gelatin mold wobbling on a plate: gelatina, jelly, Jell-O desserts
comida.drawing: A fluted gelatin mold wobbling on a plate: gelatina, jelly, Jell-O desserts
comida.why: Flan is a smooth custard dome with caramel on top. Gelatin is a fluted mold with vertical ridges and a wobble. It's a very common dessert, especially in Mexico. Risk: the ridges have to keep the two domes apart.

comida.name: chicken-wing
comida.meaning: A fried chicken wing, the flat piece with its bent joint: wings, buffalo wings, alitas, game-day menus
comida.drawing: A fried chicken wing, the flat piece with its bent joint: wings, buffalo wings, alitas, game-day menus
comida.why: The drumstick is the leg: round meat on a bone handle, and its keywords cover fried chicken but not wings. 'Wings' is a menu and delivery category of its own. Risk: it must not read as a boomerang.

comida.name: groceries-clock
comida.meaning: A grocery bag with a clock badge: a scheduled grocery delivery, a delivery window, a pickup slot
comida.drawing: A grocery bag with a clock badge: a scheduled grocery delivery, a delivery window, a pickup slot
comida.why: The same grocery bag with the engine's clock badge, a real state in grocery apps, like takeaway-cup-clock in bebidas. Comida's badge siblings stay under one in five (7 of 115).

comunicacion.name: message-draft
comunicacion.meaning: Draft message: a chat message written but not sent (a dashed bubble)
comunicacion.drawing: Draft message: a chat message written but not sent (a dashed bubble)
comunicacion.why: mail-draft is an email draft. Chat apps keep a draft message in each conversation.

comunicacion.name: video-call-missed
comunicacion.meaning: Missed video call: the video-call camera with the missed-call bounce arrow. Used for a video call nobody answered, in a call log or a notification.
comunicacion.drawing: Missed video call: the video-call camera with the missed-call bounce arrow. Used for a video call nobody answered, in a call log or a notification.
comunicacion.why: phone-missed draws the handset, which means a voice call. A missed video call needs the video-call camera with the same bounce arrow, which WhatsApp, FaceTime and Android call logs all show. video-call-incoming already puts this family on the camera. comunicacion is already over one badge in five, but this is a call state drawn as a path, like phone-missed and video-call-incoming, not an engine badge.

conduccion.name: headlight-daytime
conduccion.meaning: The daytime running lights tell-tale: a lamp with short straight rays
conduccion.drawing: The daytime running lights tell-tale: a lamp with short straight rays
conduccion.why: headlight-low, headlight-high, fog-light, and parking-lights exist, but the DRL indicator doesn't. It uses the headlight family's base. It goes beyond the quota because it comes from SF.

conduccion.name: glow-plug
conduccion.meaning: The diesel preheat warning light, a coil: wait before starting the engine
conduccion.drawing: The diesel preheat warning light, a coil: wait before starting the engine
conduccion.why: spark-plug is the part. The glow-plug coil is a dashboard tell-tale that every diesel shows.

conduccion.name: gas-station-alert
conduccion.meaning: The fuel pump with an alert: the low-fuel warning light
conduccion.drawing: The fuel pump with an alert: the low-fuel warning light
conduccion.why: The scope lists low fuel and no icon draws it. gas-station is the pump or place, and the alert badge turns it into the warning. The family head goes first; the keywords will carry 'low fuel'.

conduccion.name: hill-descent-control
conduccion.meaning: A car on a downhill slope with a down arrow: hill descent control
conduccion.drawing: A car on a downhill slope with a down arrow: hill descent control
conduccion.why: There is no hill descent indicator. traction-control is wheel slip. 'contains hills' is the landscape icon.

conduccion.name: backup-camera
conduccion.meaning: A car seen from above with a camera view fanning out behind it: the rear-view camera when reversing
conduccion.drawing: A car seen from above with a camera view fanning out behind it: the rear-view camera when reversing
conduccion.why: parking-sensor is the beeping distance aid and dash-camera (dispositivos) is a recorder. The camera view behind the car is a separate feature. The sd-card search hit is noise.

conduccion.name: power-window
conduccion.meaning: A car side window with up and down arrows: power window controls and the window lock
conduccion.drawing: A car side window with up and down arrows: power window controls and the window lock
conduccion.why: No car-window control exists. 'contains window' is the app window in ventanas.

conduccion.name: steering-wheel-lock
conduccion.meaning: A steering wheel with a padlock: steering lock engaged, anti-theft
conduccion.drawing: A steering wheel with a padlock: steering lock engaged, anti-theft
conduccion.why: steering-wheel-alert is a power-steering fault. The lock is a sibling on the same base, like steering-wheel-heated.

conduccion.name: collision-warning
conduccion.meaning: A car with a burst just ahead of it: forward collision warning
conduccion.drawing: A car with a burst just ahead of it: forward collision warning
conduccion.why: adaptive-cruise keeps a distance, and car-crash (vehiculos) is the accident after it happens. FCW is the ADAS warning beside lane-assist and blind-spot. Risk: draw one car and the burst, not two cars.

conduccion.name: ev-connector-ccs
conduccion.meaning: The CCS combo DC fast-charging plug face: filter chargers by connector
conduccion.drawing: The CCS combo DC fast-charging plug face: filter chargers by connector
conduccion.why: The family has Type 1 and Type 2 (AC) but no DC fast plug. CCS adds the two large DC pins below.

conduccion.name: ev-connector-chademo
conduccion.meaning: The CHAdeMO DC charging plug face: filter chargers by connector
conduccion.drawing: The CHAdeMO DC charging plug face: filter chargers by connector
conduccion.why: CHAdeMO has its own round face and pin layout, and charging apps list it.

conduccion.name: ev-connector-nacs
conduccion.meaning: The NACS (SAE J3400) charging plug face: filter chargers by connector
conduccion.drawing: The NACS (SAE J3400) charging plug face: filter chargers by connector
conduccion.why: This is a standard, not a brand. Its slim face is now the North American default and is missing from the family.

conduccion.name: gearbox-alert
conduccion.meaning: A gearbox with an alert: transmission fault warning
conduccion.drawing: A gearbox with an alert: transmission fault warning
conduccion.why: gearbox is the part or service. With the alert it is the fault light, matching engine-alert and steering-wheel-alert.

conduccion.name: air-distribution
conduccion.meaning: A seated driver with airflow arrows to the face and feet: climate air distribution modes
conduccion.drawing: A seated driver with airflow arrows to the face and feet: climate air distribution modes
conduccion.why: fresh-air and air-recirculation choose where the air comes from. This chooses where it goes. SF draws it in dozens of variants, and car climate screens use it. Risk: one figure with two arrows, nothing more.

conduccion.name: map-pin-fuel
conduccion.meaning: A map pin with a fuel pump inside: gas stations on a map and along a route.
conduccion.drawing: A map pin with a fuel pump inside: gas stations on a map and along a route.
conduccion.why: gas-station is the station itself. The pin marks it on a map, the Gas category every map app has.

conduccion.name: map-pin-parking
conduccion.meaning: A map pin with the parking P inside: parking lots and garages on a map.
conduccion.drawing: A map pin with the parking P inside: parking lots and garages on a map.
conduccion.why: car-location is a car with a pin badge, for the car you left somewhere. The P pin marks parking places on a map. The P is the same single-letter sign that parking already draws.

conduccion.name: side-mirror-heated
conduccion.meaning: The side mirror with heat waves: the heated-mirrors button on the dashboard and in a car app's remote climate controls.
conduccion.drawing: The side mirror with heat waves: the heated-mirrors button on the dashboard and in a car app's remote climate controls.
conduccion.why: side-mirror is the mirror itself (fold, adjust). Heating is its own control, the way steering-wheel-heated is separate from steering-wheel. The 'heated mirror' tag on side-mirror would move to it.

conduccion.name: driver-license-clock
conduccion.meaning: A driver's license with a clock badge: license expiring, renewal due (driver-document reminders in fleet and ride-hailing driver apps).
conduccion.drawing: A driver's license with a clock badge: license expiring, renewal due (driver-document reminders in fleet and ride-hailing driver apps).
conduccion.why: driver-license-check means a verified driver. The clock is the expiry reminder, as passport-clock is for the passport. license-clock in legal is a permit document, not the license card.

conduccion.name: ev-charger-check
conduccion.meaning: An EV charger with a check badge: charging complete, or the charger is available.
conduccion.drawing: An EV charger with a check badge: charging complete, or the charger is available.
conduccion.why: ev-charger-alert means out of service and ev-charger-clock means scheduled charging. The finished or available state is the one charging apps show most.

conduccion.name: car-key-plus
conduccion.meaning: A car key with a plus badge: add or share a digital car key (a phone key or a wallet car key).
conduccion.drawing: A car key with a plus badge: add or share a digital car key (a phone key or a wallet car key).
conduccion.why: key-plus is a generic credential and car-plus adds a vehicle. Adding a key to a car the person already has is a state of the car-key family.

conduccion.name: parking-check
conduccion.meaning: The parking P sign with a check badge: parking paid, session active, or spot reserved.
conduccion.drawing: The parking P sign with a check badge: parking paid, session active, or spot reserved.
conduccion.why: parking-clock is the time left and parking-ticket is the fine. A paid or booked spot is the confirmation that parking apps show.

construccion.name: junction-box
construccion.meaning: An electrical junction box with wires leaving it: wiring, electrical work
construccion.drawing: An electrical junction box with wires leaving it: wiring, electrical work
construccion.why: breaker-panel is the panel of breakers. The scope names junction boxes, the boxes where wires meet. The 'box' it contains is nucleo's product box.

construccion.name: excavation
construccion.meaning: A pit dug into the ground with its mound of soil beside it: excavation, earthworks, hole
construccion.drawing: A pit dug into the ground with its mound of soil beside it: excavation, earthworks, hole
construccion.why: groundbreaking is the shovel ceremony. The pit with its soil mound shows earthworks. Lucide's hole has no equivalent. The search hits (ruins, pickaxe, dinosaur-skull) come from archaeology keywords.

construccion.name: blueprint-clock
construccion.meaning: The blueprint with a clock badge. Used for a drawing or submittal in review, waiting for approval, in construction document control.
construccion.drawing: The blueprint with a clock badge. Used for a drawing or submittal in review, waiting for approval, in construction document control.
construccion.why: blueprint-check is the approved drawing and blueprint-edit is markup. Construction document-control and submittal tools hold drawings 'in review' before approval, which is the state between those two. The 'contains clock' conflict is just the badge family. It would be the category's third badge out of about 53.

controles.name: select-multiple
controles.meaning: Multi-select dropdown: one select box holding several chosen values as chips
controles.drawing: Multi-select dropdown: one select box holding several chosen values as chips
controles.why: select holds one value. checkbox-group lists every option instead of using a dropdown.

controles.name: select-cascade
controles.meaning: Cascading select: options picked level by level in side-by-side lists (country, then state, then city)
controles.drawing: Cascading select: options picked level by level in side-by-side lists (country, then state, then city)
controles.why: select-open is one list. The cascader opens a second list from the option chosen.

controles.name: input-copy
controles.meaning: Copy field: a read-only field with a copy button, for an API key or an invite link
controles.drawing: Copy field: a read-only field with a copy button, for an API key or an invite link
controles.why: input-lock only says the field can't be edited. This field is made to be copied, and copy and copy-check are the action, not the field.

controles.name: input-range
controles.meaning: Range fields: a minimum and a maximum field joined by a dash (price from–to filters)
controles.drawing: Range fields: a minimum and a maximum field joined by a dash (price from–to filters)
controles.why: slider-range sets the range by dragging. Here both ends are typed.

controles.name: input-card
controles.meaning: Card number field: the payment card field of a checkout form
controles.drawing: Card number field: the payment card field of a checkout form
controles.why: input-currency holds an amount. card (nucleo) is the payment method, not its form field.

controles.name: input-signature
controles.meaning: Signature field: the form field a person signs with a finger or the pointer
controles.drawing: Signature field: the form field a person signs with a finger or the pointer
controles.why: signature-line is a signature on a document line. This is the field type of form builders and e-sign forms.

controles.name: input-formula
controles.meaning: Formula field: a field whose value is calculated from other fields
controles.drawing: Formula field: a field whose value is calculated from other fields
controles.why: formula-bar is a spreadsheet's bar. This is a field type of forms and databases.

controles.name: textarea-rich
controles.meaning: Rich text field: a text area with its formatting toolbar
controles.drawing: Rich text field: a text area with its formatting toolbar
controles.why: textarea is plain multi-line text. The rich editor adds bold, lists, and links.

controles.name: button-floating-menu
controles.meaning: Speed dial: a floating action button opened into its smaller actions
controles.drawing: Speed dial: a floating action button opened into its smaller actions
controles.why: button-floating is the closed button. This is the same button opened into its menu.

controles.name: button-check
controles.meaning: Done button: a button in its success state once its action ends
controles.drawing: Done button: a button in its success state once its action ends
controles.why: button-loading is the busy state. No icon shows the state that comes after it.

controles.name: radio-group-alert
controles.meaning: Choice error: a single-choice group with a validation error
controles.drawing: Choice error: a single-choice group with a validation error
controles.why: checkbox-alert covers checkboxes only, and the scope asks for radios in every state. The family base is radio-group because radio alone is the device.

controles.name: fieldset-plus
controles.meaning: Repeatable group: add another set of the same fields (another address, another guest)
controles.drawing: Repeatable group: add another set of the same fields (another address, another guest)
controles.why: input-plus adds one field. This repeats a whole fieldset.

controles.name: form-reset
controles.meaning: Reset form: set every field back to its default
controles.drawing: Reset form: set every field back to its default
controles.why: input-clear empties one field, and reset (navegacion) is generic. This is the form's own reset.

controles.name: form-responses
controles.meaning: Form responses: the submissions a form has collected
controles.drawing: Form responses: the submissions a form has collected
controles.why: form-check is one form sent. This is the pile of answers the form's owner reads.

datos.name: chart-bar-sorted
datos.meaning: Columns sorted from shortest to tallest (Pareto, ranked values), used to sort a chart by value. The descending and horizontal versions come from flipPath and turnPath.
datos.drawing: Columns sorted from shortest to tallest (Pareto, ranked values), used to sort a chart by value. The descending and horizontal versions come from flipPath and turnPath.
datos.why: Gota's chart-bar and chart-bar-horizontal draw bars of arbitrary height, and lollipop draws stems and dots. Growth and decline (negocios) add a trend arrow. Lucide's increasing and decreasing bar and column charts (with and without axes) and SF's ascending and descending bars all need bars that rise steadily with no arrow, so none of them maps today.

datos.name: database-minus
datos.meaning: A database with a minus badge, used to remove a database or disconnect a data source.
datos.drawing: A database with a minus badge, used to remove a database or disconnect a data source.
datos.why: database-x is a state (database unavailable). Minus is the remove action that pairs with database-plus.

datos.name: chart-bar-stacked-percent
datos.meaning: 100% stacked bar chart: every bar is full height and split into its shares. Used in the chart pickers of BI tools and spreadsheets
datos.drawing: 100% stacked bar chart: every bar is full height and split into its shares. Used in the chart pickers of BI tools and spreadsheets
datos.why: In a stacked bar chart the bars have different heights because they show totals. In a 100% stacked chart every bar is the same height because it shows proportions. Excel, Sheets and Looker list it as its own chart type, and the datos scope asks for more chart kinds.

datos.name: dashboard-gear
datos.meaning: Dashboard with a gear: open the dashboard's settings (variables, refresh, permissions) in BI and monitoring tools
datos.drawing: Dashboard with a gear: open the dashboard's settings (variables, refresh, permissions) in BI and monitoring tools
datos.why: dashboard-edit rearranges the panels. The gear opens the dashboard's settings, the same way agent-gear and bell-gear do for their objects. datos has badges on only about 10% of its icons.

datos.name: data-pipeline-check
datos.meaning: Data pipeline with a check: a pipeline run or sync that succeeded, shown in ETL and orchestration tools
datos.drawing: Data pipeline with a check: a pipeline run or sync that succeeded, shown in ETL and orchestration tools
datos.why: data-pipeline already has its scheduled state (clock) and its failed state (alert), but not the succeeded state that every run list shows. ci-pipeline-check is a CI/CD build drawn on another base.

datos.name: database-pause
datos.meaning: The database with a pause badge: a database or warehouse suspended on purpose and ready to resume (a paused project, suspended compute, a suspended warehouse).
datos.drawing: The database with a pause badge: a database or warehouse suspended on purpose and ready to resume (a paused project, suspended compute, a suspended warehouse).
datos.why: database-x means unavailable (an outage or a failed connection), and database-clock means a scheduled refresh. A paused database was stopped on purpose and resumes on demand: Supabase paused projects, Neon suspended compute, Snowflake suspend/resume warehouse, Aurora auto-pause. It uses the same pause badge as wifi-pause, cloud-pause, sync-pause and download-pause. names.mjs flags 'contains pause'; that is the badge's family logic.

deportes.name: cricket-ball
deportes.meaning: A cricket ball with its single straight raised seam; cricket matches, clubs and scores.
deportes.drawing: A cricket ball with its single straight raised seam; cricket matches, clubs and scores.
deportes.why: The baseball's seam curves in a figure-eight, while a cricket ball has one straight band of stitches around the middle. Gota has no cricket ball.

deportes.name: lacrosse-stick
deportes.meaning: A lacrosse stick: a long shaft with a netted triangular head; lacrosse teams and gear.
deportes.drawing: A lacrosse stick: a long shaft with a netted triangular head; lacrosse teams and gear.
deportes.why: A hockey stick ends in a flat blade. Lacrosse is the netted head, and no Gota icon shows lacrosse.

deportes.name: water-polo
deportes.meaning: A water polo ball floating on waves; water polo matches and aquatic team sports.
deportes.drawing: A water polo ball floating on waves; water polo matches and aquatic team sports.
deportes.why: The ball alone reads as volleyball. The waves under it make it water polo, which Gota doesn't have.

deportes.name: inline-skate
deportes.meaning: An inline skate: a boot with its wheels in one row; rollerblading, rinks, rentals.
deportes.drawing: An inline skate: a boot with its wheels in one row; rollerblading, rinks, rentals.
deportes.why: roller-skate is the quad skate, two pairs of wheels (its tags say quad skate and roller disco). An inline skate has its wheels in one line.

deportes.name: bobsled
deportes.meaning: A bobsled in profile on its runners; bobsleigh, luge and other sliding events.
deportes.drawing: A bobsled in profile on its runners; bobsleigh, luge and other sliding events.
deportes.why: sled (camping) is a kids' toboggan. The bobsled is the closed racing capsule of the sliding sports.

deportes.name: air-horn
deportes.meaning: A handheld air horn: a canister with a flared horn; fans at games, race starts.
deportes.drawing: A handheld air horn: a canister with a flared horn; fans at games, race starts.
deportes.why: The megaphone is for speaking and announcements. The air horn is the canister noisemaker fans use and races start with.

deportes.name: championship-belt
deportes.meaning: A boxing or wrestling title belt with its big central plate; champions, title fights.
deportes.drawing: A boxing or wrestling title belt with its big central plate; champions, title fights.
deportes.why: belt (ropa) is a trouser belt with a buckle. The title belt is a wide strap with a plate, the prize itself. names.mjs flags it as containing belt because they share that word, but they are different objects.

deportes.name: martial-arts-belt
deportes.meaning: A martial-arts belt tied in its knot with two hanging ends; karate and judo ranks, grading.
deportes.drawing: A martial-arts belt tied in its knot with two hanging ends; karate and judo ranks, grading.
deportes.why: martial-arts is the kicking figure, and belt (ropa) is a buckled trouser belt. Ranks and grading need the knotted belt.

deportes.name: ice-rink
deportes.meaning: An ice rink from above, with rounded corners, a center line and a circle; skating sessions, hockey arenas.
deportes.drawing: An ice rink from above, with rounded corners, a center line and a circle; skating sessions, hockey arenas.
deportes.why: ice-skating is the skater. The rink is the venue, the way soccer-field sits beside soccer-player. The scope lists rinks.

deportes.name: running-track
deportes.meaning: An athletics track from above: two lanes around an open infield; track and field venues.
deportes.drawing: An athletics track from above: two lanes around an open infield; track and field venues.
deportes.why: hurdle is the barrier, and the scope's track venue has no icon. Risk: draw only two lanes with straight sides so it never reads as a target.

deportes.name: race-track
deportes.meaning: A motor-racing circuit outline with a checkered start line; circuits, race calendars.
deportes.drawing: A motor-racing circuit outline with a checkered start line; circuits, race calendars.
deportes.why: checkered-flag marks the finish. The circuit is the motorsport venue. Risk: the outline must keep long straights so it doesn't read as a scribble.

deportes.name: ski-slope
deportes.meaning: A mountain slope with a ski run and a piste marker; ski resorts, slope status.
deportes.drawing: A mountain slope with a ski run and a piste marker; ski resorts, slope status.
deportes.why: skiing is the skier, with 'slopes' only as a tag. The slope is the venue that resort apps show status for, as a field sits beside its player.

deportes.name: volleyball-player
deportes.meaning: A figure jumping to spike a volleyball overhead; volleyball teams and matches.
deportes.drawing: A figure jumping to spike a volleyball overhead; volleyball teams and matches.
deportes.why: The ball alone. The -player family has soccer, basketball, tennis and hockey but no volleyball figure.

deportes.name: golf-player
deportes.meaning: A golfer at the end of the swing, club over the shoulder; golf lessons, tee times.
deportes.drawing: A golfer at the end of the swing, club over the shoulder; golf lessons, tee times.
deportes.why: Golf has its ball, club, bag and course in Gota but no figure.

deportes.name: table-tennis-player
deportes.meaning: A figure at a table tennis table striking with a small paddle; ping-pong clubs.
deportes.drawing: A figure at a table tennis table striking with a small paddle; ping-pong clubs.
deportes.why: tennis-player is on a court with a full racket. The table and the small paddle make it table tennis. The name contains tennis-player only through the -player family.

deportes.name: badminton-player
deportes.meaning: A figure smashing a shuttlecock overhead with a light racket; badminton.
deportes.drawing: A figure smashing a shuttlecock overhead with a light racket; badminton.
deportes.why: The shuttlecock overhead makes it badminton. Gota has the shuttlecock and the racket but no figure.

deportes.name: american-football-player
deportes.meaning: A helmeted figure throwing an American football; football teams, fantasy rosters.
deportes.drawing: A helmeted figure throwing an American football; football teams, fantasy rosters.
deportes.why: The helmet and the ball exist on their own. The throwing figure completes the -player family.

deportes.name: rugby-player
deportes.meaning: A figure running with a rugby ball held in both hands; rugby matches.
deportes.drawing: A figure running with a rugby ball held in both hands; rugby matches.
deportes.why: Gota has only the ball. Carrying it in both hands while running is what reads as rugby.

deportes.name: cricket-player
deportes.meaning: A padded batter swinging a flat cricket bat low, the wicket behind; cricket.
deportes.drawing: A padded batter swinging a flat cricket bat low, the wicket behind; cricket.
deportes.why: baseball-player bats upright with a round bat. The flat bat, the pads and the wicket make it cricket.

deportes.name: handball-player
deportes.meaning: A figure leaping to throw a handball one-handed; handball matches.
deportes.drawing: A figure leaping to throw a handball one-handed; handball matches.
deportes.why: Gota has nothing for handball. The one-handed jump throw is the sport's signature pose.

deportes.name: bowling-player
deportes.meaning: A figure in the low bowling delivery, releasing the ball; bowling leagues.
deportes.drawing: A figure in the low bowling delivery, releasing the ball; bowling leagues.
deportes.why: Gota has only the ball and the pin. The low delivery is the bowler.

deportes.name: cross-country-skiing
deportes.meaning: A skier striding on flat snow with both poles; Nordic skiing, trails.
deportes.drawing: A skier striding on flat snow with both poles; Nordic skiing, trails.
deportes.why: skiing is labeled Downhill skiing. Nordic skiing strides on the flat, and the name contains skiing as its family.

deportes.name: ski-jumping
deportes.meaning: A ski jumper in flight, leaning over skis spread in a V; ski jumping.
deportes.drawing: A ski jumper in flight, leaning over skis spread in a V; ski jumping.
deportes.why: The jumper in the air with the skis in a V is its own event, not a descent.

deportes.name: kitesurfing
deportes.meaning: A rider on a board pulled by a kite on lines overhead; kitesurfing, kiteboarding.
deportes.drawing: A rider on a board pulled by a kite on lines overhead; kitesurfing, kiteboarding.
deportes.why: Windsurfing's sail is fixed to the board, and it carries kitesurfing only as a tag. A kite flying on lines is a different sport.

deportes.name: paddleboarding
deportes.meaning: A figure standing on a board, pushing with a long single paddle; stand-up paddle.
deportes.drawing: A figure standing on a board, pushing with a long single paddle; stand-up paddle.
deportes.why: Surfing rides a wave. Kayak (nautica) is seated with a double paddle. Stand-up paddle is standing on flat water, and the scope lists paddles.

deportes.name: bungee-jumping
deportes.meaning: A figure diving head-down on an elastic cord; bungee jumps, adventure parks.
deportes.drawing: A figure diving head-down on an elastic cord; bungee jumps, adventure parks.
deportes.why: parachute is skydiving, and bungee-cord (herramientas) is a strap. The head-down fall on a cord is the extreme sport.

deportes.name: scuba-diving
deportes.meaning: A diver swimming with a tank and fins; scuba courses, dive trips.
deportes.drawing: A diver swimming with a tank and fins; scuba courses, dive trips.
deportes.why: scuba-mask (nautica) is labeled Mask and snorkel, the snorkeling gear. The diver with a tank is scuba diving.

deportes.name: fencing
deportes.meaning: A masked fencer lunging with a foil; fencing clubs and bouts.
deportes.drawing: A masked fencer lunging with a foil; fencing clubs and bouts.
deportes.why: Gota has no fencing. The foil counts as sports equipment, which the taxonomy allows, and the mask and lunge read as sport, not a weapon. The judge should confirm.

deportes.name: pole-vault
deportes.meaning: A vaulter on a bending pole clearing the bar; pole vault.
deportes.drawing: A vaulter on a bending pole clearing the bar; pole vault.
deportes.why: The bending pole is what reads. The vault in comercio is a bank vault and doesn't overlap.

deportes.name: shot-put
deportes.meaning: A figure pushing a heavy ball from the shoulder; shot put, throwing events.
deportes.drawing: A figure pushing a heavy ball from the shoulder; shot put, throwing events.
deportes.why: Gota has no throwing event. The ball held at the neck is the shot put.

deportes.name: wheelchair-racing
deportes.meaning: A racing wheelchair with its long front wheel, the athlete bent forward; para athletics.
deportes.drawing: A racing wheelchair with its long front wheel, the athlete bent forward; para athletics.
deportes.why: wheelchair-basketball is the team sport, and wheelchair (accesibilidad) is everyday use. The three-wheeled racing chair is para athletics.

deportes.name: cheerleader
deportes.meaning: A figure with arms raised in a V, holding pom-poms; cheerleading squads.
deportes.drawing: A figure with arms raised in a V, holding pom-poms; cheerleading squads.
deportes.why: foam-finger is a fan. Cheerleading is a sport and a squad role, and no icon or tag covers it.

deportes.name: rowing
deportes.meaning: A rower in a narrow racing shell pulling two long oars, in profile; rowing clubs, regattas.
deportes.drawing: A rower in a narrow racing shell pulling two long oars, in profile; rowing clubs, regattas.
deportes.why: rowboat (nautica) is a leisure dinghy, and rowing-machine (fitness) is the indoor erg. The racing shell is the Olympic sport.

deportes.name: tennis-court-clock
deportes.meaning: A tennis or padel court with a clock badge: book a court and pick a time slot (Playtomic, CourtReserve, club apps).
deportes.drawing: A tennis or padel court with a clock badge: book a court and pick a time slot (Playtomic, CourtReserve, club apps).
deportes.why: soccer-field-clock is booking a pitch. Racket courts (tennis, padel, pickleball) are the largest court-booking market and draw on another base, tennis-court, so the booking state needs that base. It follows the family's logic of soccer-field-clock. Deportes has only 1 badge in about 126 icons.

desarrollo.name: git-branch-minus
desarrollo.meaning: The branch with a minus badge, used to delete a branch.
desarrollo.drawing: The branch with a minus badge, used to delete a branch.
desarrollo.why: The branch family has new, protected, and update, but no delete.

desarrollo.name: git-bisect
desarrollo.meaning: A line of commits with one singled out under a magnifier: git bisect, finding the commit that introduced a bug.
desarrollo.drawing: A line of commits with one singled out under a magnifier: git bisect, finding the commit that introduced a bug.
desarrollo.why: git-graph is the commit history, and code-search searches files. Bisect is its own version-control operation, in scope beside rebase, cherry-pick, and stash.

desarrollo.name: inspect-element
desarrollo.meaning: A dashed box with the pointer on its corner: inspect element, the DevTools element picker.
desarrollo.drawing: A dashed box with the pointer on its corner: inspect element, the DevTools element picker.
desarrollo.why: accessibility-search is the accessibility inspector, and selection (edicion) is a design-tool selection. Neither is the browser's generic element picker.

desarrollo.name: block-code
desarrollo.meaning: Two interlocking code blocks for visual, block-based, low-code programming.
desarrollo.drawing: Two interlocking code blocks for visual, block-based, low-code programming.
desarrollo.why: building-blocks (juegos) are toy cubes, code is text code, puzzle is an extension, and widgets are UI. Gota has nothing for block-based or low-code programming.

desarrollo.name: globe-code
desarrollo.meaning: The globe with the code sign, used for web development and website code.
desarrollo.drawing: The globe with the code sign, used for web development and website code.
desarrollo.why: code-window is the editor and server-web is hosting. Web development as a service or skill (the counterpart of a website) has no icon.

desarrollo.name: dependency-alert
desarrollo.meaning: The dependency package with an alert badge, used for a vulnerable or deprecated dependency or a security advisory.
desarrollo.drawing: The dependency package with an alert badge, used for a vulnerable or deprecated dependency or a security advisory.
desarrollo.why: dependency-arrow-up is the upgrade itself. The alert is the step before it (a Dependabot-style vulnerability alert), and it isn't circular-dependency's build warning.

desarrollo.name: ssh-key
desarrollo.meaning: A key with the terminal prompt: an SSH key or deploy key, used to reach a server or push to a repository.
desarrollo.drawing: A key with the terminal prompt: an SSH key or deploy key, used to reach a server or push to a repository.
desarrollo.why: api-key is a token for an API, and git-clone only mentions SSH among its keywords. The SSH credential has its own place in every Git host's and cloud's settings.

dispositivos.name: desktop-x
dispositivos.meaning: The desktop monitor with an x badge, used when a display isn't detected, a computer is offline, or a device has been removed.
dispositivos.drawing: The desktop monitor with an x badge, used when a display isn't detected, a computer is offline, or a device has been removed.
dispositivos.why: The desktop family has no failure state. laptop-check and laptop-lock are states of the laptop, and server-x is the server. SF's display with a warning badge says the same.

dispositivos.name: desktop-gear
dispositivos.meaning: The desktop monitor with a gear badge, used for computer or display settings and system preferences.
dispositivos.drawing: The desktop monitor with a gear badge, used for computer or display settings and system preferences.
dispositivos.why: smartphone-gear is the phone's settings. network-gear and gear are generic. Nothing names the computer's own settings.

dispositivos.name: wifi-gear
dispositivos.meaning: The Wi-Fi fan with a gear badge, used for Wi-Fi settings and to configure the wireless network.
dispositivos.drawing: The Wi-Fi fan with a gear badge, used for Wi-Fi settings and to configure the wireless network.
dispositivos.why: network-gear is the node graph (IP, DNS, proxy settings). The wifi family has lock, alert, pause, and guest badges but no settings.

dispositivos.name: wifi-sync
dispositivos.meaning: The Wi-Fi fan with the sync badge, used while reconnecting to Wi-Fi or refreshing the connection.
dispositivos.drawing: The Wi-Fi fan with the sync badge, used while reconnecting to Wi-Fi or refreshing the connection.
dispositivos.why: wifi-alert is an error (no internet). Reconnecting is a passing state, as cloud-sync is beside cloud-alert.

dispositivos.name: tracker-tag
dispositivos.meaning: A round Bluetooth tag on a key ring with signal arcs: an item tracker to find keys, bags, or a wallet.
dispositivos.drawing: A round Bluetooth tag on a key ring with signal arcs: an item tracker to find keys, bags, or a wallet.
