nautica.drawing: An inflatable boat (RIB) with its tubes and an outboard: dinghies, tenders, and boat tours
nautica.why: rowboat is rigid and boat is a motorboat. The tubes and the motor keep it from being the low empty hull round 8 dropped.

nautica.name: airboat
nautica.meaning: A flat airboat with a big caged fan at the stern: swamp and wetland tours
nautica.drawing: A flat airboat with a big caged fan at the stern: swamp and wetland tours
nautica.why: The caged fan is what makes it this boat, so it isn't a bare low hull.

nautica.name: hydrofoil
nautica.meaning: A hydrofoil ferry raised on its foils above the water: fast ferries
nautica.drawing: A hydrofoil ferry raised on its foils above the water: fast ferries
nautica.why: The hull lifted on struts is a kind of its own, used on fast passenger routes.

nautica.name: map-pin-anchor
nautica.meaning: A map pin with an anchor: harbor, anchorage, or mooring location
nautica.drawing: A map pin with an anchor: harbor, anchorage, or mooring location
nautica.why: The map-pin family marks places by type (plane, bus, train, tent, bird, paw) but has no harbor or anchorage. marina is the place itself, not its pin.

navegacion.name: sort-a-z
navegacion.meaning: Sort A to Z: alphabetical order
navegacion.drawing: Sort A to Z: alphabetical order
navegacion.why: sort-ascending is drawn with bars and sorts by value. The letters say the sort is alphabetical. sort-a-z and sort-z-a share their words on purpose, since the order of the words is the direction.

navegacion.name: sort-z-a
navegacion.meaning: Sort Z to A: reverse alphabetical order
navegacion.drawing: Sort Z to A: reverse alphabetical order
navegacion.why: The same reason as sort-a-z, in reverse. The letters swap places, so a flip of the drawing can't make it.

navegacion.name: sort-0-9
navegacion.meaning: Sort 0 to 9: numeric order, low to high
navegacion.drawing: Sort 0 to 9: numeric order, low to high
navegacion.why: The digits say the sort is numeric. It pairs with sort-9-0.

navegacion.name: sort-9-0
navegacion.meaning: Sort 9 to 0: numeric order, high to low
navegacion.drawing: Sort 9 to 0: numeric order, high to low
navegacion.why: The same reason as sort-0-9, in reverse.

navegacion.name: arrow-turn-left-down
navegacion.meaning: An arrow going left, then turning down
navegacion.drawing: An arrow going left, then turning down
navegacion.why: In the arrow-turn family the word order is the path. arrow-turn-down-left (Enter) goes down, then left, and ends pointing left. This arrow ends pointing down. If the shared words are confusing, rename it arrow-corner-left-down.

navegacion.name: arrow-turn-right-down
navegacion.meaning: An arrow going right, then turning down
navegacion.drawing: An arrow going right, then turning down
navegacion.why: The same reason as arrow-turn-left-down. arrow-turn-down-right (Indent) ends pointing right. The Heroicons name is the same.

navegacion.name: rows
navegacion.meaning: Rows: a layout of stacked horizontal bands
navegacion.drawing: Rows: a layout of stacked horizontal bands
navegacion.why: columns (nucleo) splits a frame into columns, and rows is the same drawing turned. view-list is a list with bullets.

navegacion.name: columns-gear
navegacion.meaning: Customize columns: choose and order the columns of a table
navegacion.drawing: Customize columns: choose and order the columns of a table
navegacion.why: columns shows the table. Choosing which columns appear is the column picker every data table has.

navegacion.name: scale-3d
navegacion.meaning: Scale in 3D: resize an object along its axes
navegacion.drawing: Scale in 3D: resize an object along its axes
navegacion.why: rotate-3d exists but its scale counterpart doesn't. axis-3d (datos) is the axes alone.

navegacion.name: search-check
navegacion.meaning: Match found: the search found what was asked
navegacion.drawing: Match found: the search found what was asked
navegacion.why: search-x is no results, and this is its pair.

navegacion.name: mouse-middle-click
navegacion.meaning: The mouse with its scroll wheel pressed and click rays above it: middle click, for input instructions, shortcut help and button mapping (open in new tab, pan in CAD and 3D tools).
navegacion.drawing: The mouse with its scroll wheel pressed and click rays above it: middle click, for input instructions, shortcut help and button mapping (open in new tab, pan in CAD and 3D tools).
navegacion.why: mouse-left-click and mouse-right-click exist and this is the third button of the family. mouse-scroll (dispositivos) shows the wheel rolling with arrows, not a press.

navegacion.name: tabs-x
navegacion.meaning: The tabbed window with an x badge: close a tab, the Close tab and Close other tabs commands in browsers and tabbed apps.
navegacion.drawing: The tabbed window with an x badge: close a tab, the Close tab and Close other tabs commands in browsers and tabbed apps.
navegacion.why: tabs-plus opens a tab and window-x closes the whole window. Browsers list Close tab and Close window as separate commands. A real state on a managed object; navegacion has only 4% badges.

navegacion.name: filter-star
navegacion.meaning: Saved filter: the funnel with a star badge, for a set of filters that is starred or saved to apply again (saved filters and views in issue trackers, mail and stores).
navegacion.drawing: Saved filter: the funnel with a star badge, for a set of filters that is starred or saved to apply again (saved filters and views in issue trackers, mail and stores).
navegacion.why: filter-plus creates a filter and filter-x clears it, but nothing marks a filter as kept. Issue trackers (starred filters) and stores (saved searches) show that state. It follows task-star, folder-star and file-star. Badges are only 4.5% of navegacion. The contains hit on star is the badge.

navegacion.name: search-star
navegacion.meaning: Saved search: the magnifier with the engine's star glyph badge. Used for a search kept to run again or to send alerts about new matches (jobs, homes, listings, products).
navegacion.drawing: Saved search: the magnifier with the engine's star glyph badge. Used for a search kept to run again or to send alerts about new matches (jobs, homes, listings, products).
navegacion.why: search-check (approved in pass 1, 'Match found') and search-x ('No results') show the outcome of a search. A saved search is a search the person keeps, as in Zillow saved searches, LinkedIn and Indeed job alerts, and eBay saved searches. No icon covers it: find.mjs 'saved search' returns only search and its object badges. Put the star as the engine's glyph badge, not inside the lens: under about 8 wide inside the lens it turns to mush.

negocios.name: target-x
negocios.meaning: Goal missed: the target with an x badge, an objective or OKR that closed unmet
negocios.drawing: Goal missed: the target with an x badge, an objective or OKR that closed unmet
negocios.why: target-alert is a goal at risk and still open; this one ended unmet. It completes target-plus, -alert and -progress. 'Goal reached' already exists as flag-check, so no target-check.

negocios.name: deal-clock
negocios.meaning: Deal pending: the handshake with a clock badge, a deal still in negotiation
negocios.drawing: Deal pending: the handshake with a clock badge, a deal still in negotiation
negocios.why: deal-check and deal-x are won and lost. The open deal, the third state every CRM pipeline shows, has no icon.

negocios.name: supplier-plus
negocios.meaning: Add supplier: the supplier factory and arrow with a plus badge
negocios.drawing: Add supplier: the supplier factory and arrow with a plus badge
negocios.why: supplier has approved (check) and find (search), but not the add action that vendor lists need

negocios.name: acquisition
negocios.meaning: Acquisition: a small office building pulled by an arrow into a large one
negocios.drawing: Acquisition: a small office building pulled by an arrow into a large one
negocios.why: merger shows two companies converging as equals into a third; an acquisition is one company absorbing a smaller one, in one direction

negocios.name: spin-off
negocios.meaning: Spin-off: a small office building splitting away from a large one along an arrow (divestiture)
negocios.drawing: Spin-off: a small office building splitting away from a large one along an arrow (divestiture)
negocios.why: office-branches links branches that stay with the headquarters; a spin-off is a part leaving to become its own company, the reverse of an acquisition

negocios.name: enterprise
negocios.meaning: Enterprise: a cluster of office buildings of different heights, a corporate group or an enterprise account or plan
negocios.drawing: Enterprise: a cluster of office buildings of different heights, a corporate group or an enterprise account or plan
negocios.why: office-branches is a headquarters linked to branches and skyscraper is one tower. Lucide's building-complex is a group of buildings read as one organization.

negocios.name: handshake-heart
negocios.meaning: Trusted partnership: a handshake inside a heart, for charity, community and care partnerships
negocios.drawing: Trusted partnership: a handshake inside a heart, for charity, community and care partnerships
negocios.why: the plain handshake means a deal; with the heart it means a partnership built on trust or a charitable one

negocios.name: burn-rate
negocios.meaning: Burn rate: a banknote with a flame at its corner, the cash a company spends each month
negocios.drawing: Burn rate: a banknote with a flame at its corner, the cash a company spends each month
negocios.why: money-wings is personal spending. Burn rate is the startup metric of cash consumed against runway, a KPI on its own.

negocios.name: cost-cutting
negocios.meaning: Cost cutting: scissors cutting through a banknote, cost reduction
negocios.drawing: Cost cutting: scissors cutting through a banknote, cost reduction
negocios.why: revenue-down is income falling; cost cutting is a deliberate cut in expenses, the opposite lever

negocios.name: market-share
negocios.meaning: Market share: a pie with one slice pulled out, the share a company holds of its market
negocios.drawing: Market share: a pie with one slice pulled out, the share a company holds of its market
negocios.why: chart-pie is a generic chart. market-size shows TAM/SAM/SOM as nested circles, and neither names the share one company holds.

negocios.name: purchase-requisition
negocios.meaning: Purchase request: a clipboard with a shopping cart, the internal request to buy that comes before a purchase order
negocios.drawing: Purchase request: a clipboard with a shopping cart, the internal request to buy that comes before a purchase order
negocios.why: the purchase order goes out to the supplier; the requisition is the internal procurement step before it, approved inside the company

negocios.name: value-proposition
negocios.meaning: Value proposition: an open hand presenting a gem, what a business offers its customer
negocios.drawing: Value proposition: an open hand presenting a gem, what a business offers its customer
negocios.why: differentiation is one dot standing out in a grid of dots; the value proposition is the offer itself. business-canvas is the whole model.

oficina.name: decimal-increase
oficina.meaning: Increase decimals: show more decimal places in a cell
oficina.drawing: Increase decimals: show more decimal places in a cell
oficina.why: This is a number-format button from the spreadsheet toolbar, and no Gota icon changes a cell's precision.

oficina.name: decimal-decrease
oficina.meaning: Decrease decimals: show fewer decimal places in a cell
oficina.drawing: Decrease decimals: show fewer decimal places in a cell
oficina.why: It pairs with decimal-increase, the other half of the same spreadsheet control.

oficina.name: conditional-format
oficina.meaning: Conditional formatting: cells styled by a rule
oficina.drawing: Conditional formatting: cells styled by a rule
oficina.why: paint-roller copies formatting. Conditional formatting applies it by a rule.

oficina.name: data-validation
oficina.meaning: Data validation: a rule that limits what a cell accepts (a list, a range)
oficina.drawing: Data validation: a rule that limits what a cell accepts (a list, a range)
oficina.why: form-alert shows a form's errors. This is a spreadsheet rule set on a cell.

oficina.name: ballpoint-pen
oficina.meaning: Ballpoint pen: the everyday click pen on the desk
oficina.drawing: Ballpoint pen: the everyday click pen on the desk
oficina.why: The set has pencils, the pen tool, and the fountain pen (legal). The everyday pen with a clip isn't drawn.

oficina.name: index-card
oficina.meaning: Index card: a ruled card for notes and study
oficina.drawing: Index card: a ruled card for notes and study
oficina.why: A sticky note is square and adhesive. The index card is the wider ruled card of card files and study decks.

oficina.name: task-recurring
oficina.meaning: Recurring task: a to-do that repeats
oficina.drawing: Recurring task: a to-do that repeats
oficina.why: calendar-repeat is a recurring event. Task managers repeat tasks without a calendar.

oficina.name: printer-plus
oficina.meaning: Printer with a plus: add a printer in system settings and office apps
oficina.drawing: Printer with a plus: add a printer in system settings and office apps
oficina.why: printer-check means printing is done and printer-alert means a printer error. Adding a printer to the device is a separate action in every operating system's printer settings. The printer badges live in oficina, where about 11% of icons have a badge.

oficina.name: task-clock
oficina.meaning: The task card with a clock badge: a to-do with a due time or a reminder set, for scheduled tasks and reminder lists in to-do apps.
oficina.drawing: The task card with a clock badge: a to-do with a due time or a reminder set, for scheduled tasks and reminder lists in to-do apps.
oficina.why: calendar-due is a deadline on the calendar and clock-alert means overdue. This is the task itself with a time on it (Microsoft To Do reminders, Todoist due times). The search hits agent-clock (a scheduled AI agent) and terminal-clock (a cron job) are different objects. oficina goes from 12% badges to 14%.

oficina.name: meeting-room-check
oficina.meaning: The meeting room with a check badge: room booked, a confirmed room reservation in room-booking and calendar apps.
oficina.drawing: The meeting room with a check badge: room booked, a confirmed room reservation in room-booking and calendar apps.
oficina.why: meeting-room is the room and the act of booking it. The check is the confirmed booking, the same state desk-check (rrhh) gives a desk. The 'contains room/check' conflict is the badge on its own family base.

personas.name: surgeon
personas.meaning: Bust in a surgical cap and mask: surgeon, surgical team
personas.drawing: Bust in a surgical cap and mask: surgeon, surgical team
personas.why: The doctor is told by the stethoscope. The surgeon is told by the cap and mask, and is used for surgical teams and specialties.

personas.name: paramedic
personas.meaning: Bust with a first-aid bag at its side: paramedic, EMS crew, first responder
personas.drawing: Bust with a first-aid bag at its side: paramedic, EMS crew, first responder
personas.why: The nurse is ward care, even though it is tagged medic. The paramedic is field EMS, told by the bag. Drop it if the nurse's tags are enough.

personas.name: lifeguard
personas.meaning: Bust with a rescue tube: lifeguard at a pool or beach
personas.drawing: Bust with a rescue tube: lifeguard at a pool or beach
personas.why: The tower (lugares) is the place. This is the person on duty.

personas.name: bartender
personas.meaning: Bust with a cocktail shaker: bartender, mixologist
personas.drawing: Bust with a cocktail shaker: bartender, mixologist
personas.why: The waiter (restaurante) serves tables. The bartender is told by the shaker. cocktail-shaker is only the object.

personas.name: barista
personas.meaning: Bust with a coffee cup: barista, coffee shop staff
personas.drawing: Bust with a coffee cup: barista, coffee shop staff
personas.why: shop-assistant is a generic store clerk. The barista is told by the cup and is used for cafés.

personas.name: baker
personas.meaning: Bust with a loaf of bread: baker, bakery staff
personas.drawing: Bust with a loaf of bread: baker, bakery staff
personas.why: The chef (cocina) is the kitchen with the toque. The baker carries the loaf and is used for bakeries.

personas.name: carpenter
personas.meaning: Bust with a hand saw: carpenter, woodworker
personas.drawing: Bust with a hand saw: carpenter, woodworker
personas.why: builder is the hard-hat site worker. The carpenter is told by the saw.

personas.name: welder
personas.meaning: Bust under a raised welding helmet: welder, metalworker
personas.drawing: Bust under a raised welding helmet: welder, metalworker
personas.why: welding-mask (seguridad-laboral) is the PPE alone. This is the trade, worn by the person.

personas.name: miner
personas.meaning: Bust in a hard hat with a lamp: miner
personas.drawing: Bust in a hard hat with a lamp: miner
personas.why: hard-hat-lamp (seguridad-laboral) is the gear alone. This is the worker.

personas.name: fisher
personas.meaning: Bust with a fishing rod: fisher, angler, fishing guide
personas.drawing: Bust with a fishing rod: fisher, angler, fishing guide
personas.why: No person with a rod exists. The fishing gear in camping has no person.

personas.name: sailor
personas.meaning: Bust in a captain hat: sailor, skipper, ship crew
personas.drawing: Bust in a captain hat: sailor, skipper, ship crew
personas.why: The pilot is aviation. captain-hat (nautica) is the hat alone.

personas.name: interpreter
personas.meaning: Bust with two speech bubbles: spoken-language interpreter, translator
personas.drawing: Bust with two speech bubbles: spoken-language interpreter, translator
personas.why: That one signs. This one is spoken language, and translate (comunicacion) has no person.

personas.name: gamer
personas.meaning: Bust with a gamepad: gamer, player profile
personas.drawing: Bust with a gamepad: gamer, player profile
personas.why: listener is audio with headphones. The gamer is told by the gamepad and is used for player profiles and esports.

personas.name: referee
personas.meaning: Bust with a whistle: referee, umpire, match official
personas.drawing: Bust with a whistle: referee, umpire, match official
personas.why: referee-shirt (deportes) is the garment. This is the official as a person.

personas.name: waste-collector
personas.meaning: Bust with a wheeled bin: garbage collector, sanitation worker
personas.drawing: Bust with a wheeled bin: garbage collector, sanitation worker
personas.why: cleaner is indoor cleaning. This is municipal waste collection, told by the wheeled bin.

personas.name: architect
personas.meaning: Bust with a set square: architect
personas.drawing: Bust with a set square: architect
personas.why: designer is digital and graphic design. blueprint and drafting-table have no person.

personas.name: locksmith
personas.meaning: Bust with a key: locksmith
personas.drawing: Bust with a key: locksmith
personas.why: technician is generic repair. The locksmith is told by the key and is used in home-service apps.

personas.name: tailor
personas.meaning: Bust with a tape measure around the neck: tailor, alterations
personas.drawing: Bust with a tape measure around the neck: tailor, alterations
personas.why: The sewing tools in ropa have no person. The tape around the neck tells the trade.

personas.name: makeup-artist
personas.meaning: Bust with a makeup brush: makeup artist, beauty pro
personas.drawing: Bust with a makeup brush: makeup artist, beauty pro
personas.why: hairstylist is hair. The name contains arte's 'artist' (a painter) only because the trade is called 'makeup artist'.

personas.name: actor
personas.meaning: Bust with a theater mask: actor, performer, cast
personas.drawing: Bust with a theater mask: actor, performer, cast
personas.why: musician is music. The actor is told by the mask.

personas.name: dj
personas.meaning: Bust in headphones with a record: DJ
personas.drawing: Bust in headphones with a record: DJ
personas.why: listener only listens. The DJ plays, told by the record. turntable and dj-controller are equipment.

personas.name: veterinarian
personas.meaning: Bust with a paw: veterinarian, vet staff
personas.drawing: Bust with a paw: veterinarian, vet staff
personas.why: vet (mascotas) is the service mark (a cross with paw toes), not a person. The split is the same as healthcare and doctor.

personas.name: nutritionist
personas.meaning: Bust with an apple: nutritionist, dietitian
personas.drawing: Bust with an apple: nutritionist, dietitian
personas.why: doctor is general medicine. The nutritionist is told by the apple and is used in diet and wellness apps.

personas.name: figure-bowing
personas.meaning: Whole figure bowing at the waist, in profile: bow, greeting, thanks, apology
personas.drawing: Whole figure bowing at the waist, in profile: bow, greeting, thanks, apology
personas.why: No bow exists. It is a single standing figure in profile, so it reads.

personas.name: figure-shrugging
personas.meaning: Whole figure with elbows out and palms up: shrug, not sure, no idea
personas.drawing: Whole figure with elbows out and palms up: shrug, not sure, no idea
personas.why: arms-raised celebrates with the arms up in a V. The shrug has the elbows out and the palms up at the shoulders.

personas.name: figure-pointing
personas.meaning: Whole figure pointing to one side: look here, directions, show the way
personas.drawing: Whole figure pointing to one side: look here, directions, show the way
personas.why: presenter (oficina) points at a board. This is a figure pointing aside, for directions.

personas.name: figure-pulling
personas.meaning: Whole figure leaning back pulling a handle: pull, drag a load
personas.drawing: Whole figure leaning back pulling a handle: pull, drag a load
personas.why: It is the opposite action, leaning back on a handle. The scope lists actions.

personas.name: figure-crutches
personas.meaning: Whole figure walking on crutches: injured person, limited mobility
personas.drawing: Whole figure walking on crutches: injured person, limited mobility
personas.why: crutch (salud) is the object alone. This is the injured person walking on them.

plantas.name: tree-birch
plantas.meaning: A birch: a slender, pale trunk marked with dark bands under a light crown. Used for trees by kind.
plantas.drawing: A birch: a slender, pale trunk marked with dark bands under a light crown. Used for trees by kind.
plantas.why: The scope names the birch, and no tree in the set has its slim banded trunk. Keep the bands few and short so they don't read as dots.

plantas.name: tree-mangrove
plantas.meaning: A mangrove standing on arching stilt roots above the water. Used for trees by kind, coasts, and wetlands.
plantas.drawing: A mangrove standing on arching stilt roots above the water. Used for trees by kind, coasts, and wetlands.
plantas.why: roots is a plant's root system underground and wetland is a landscape. The stilt roots over water tell the mangrove, and it's a common conservation subject.

plantas.name: tree-autumn
plantas.meaning: A tree shedding its leaves, a few of them falling beside it. Used for autumn.
plantas.drawing: A tree shedding its leaves, a few of them falling beside it. Used for autumn.
plantas.why: tree-blossom is spring and tree-bare is winter. season-autumn is a single falling leaf. This completes the seasonal tree. The search hits are only 'autumn' keywords on leaves.

plantas.name: tumbleweed
plantas.meaning: A tumbleweed: a round tangle of dry stems rolling, with motion lines. Used for the desert, the West, and the 'nothing here' empty state.
plantas.drawing: A tumbleweed: a round tangle of dry stems rolling, with motion lines. Used for the desert, the West, and the 'nothing here' empty state.
plantas.why: No icon says desert drift or an empty result this way. The motion lines and open tangle keep it from reading as a ball of yarn.

plantas.name: bird-of-paradise
plantas.meaning: A bird of paradise flower: a beak-like bract with a crest of pointed petals. Used for flowers by kind and tropical gardens.
plantas.drawing: A bird of paradise flower: a beak-like bract with a crest of pointed petals. Used for flowers by kind and tropical gardens.
plantas.why: Those are open round blooms. This one's beak-and-crest profile is a shape no other flower has.

plantas.name: potted-cactus
plantas.meaning: A small round cactus in a pot. Used for houseplants and low-maintenance plants.
plantas.drawing: A small round cactus in a pot. Used for houseplants and low-maintenance plants.
plantas.why: cactus (adopted from lugares) is the desert saguaro, and succulent is an echeveria rosette. This is the cactus as a houseplant, in the potted-* family (potted-plant, potted-sprout). names.mjs flags 'contains cactus'.

plantas.name: hedge-shears
plantas.meaning: Hedge shears with long straight blades and long handles. Used for trimming hedges and gardening tools.
plantas.drawing: Hedge shears with long straight blades and long handles. Used for trimming hedges and gardening tools.
plantas.why: These are the two-handed long-bladed tool. hedge is the plant itself.

plantas.name: plant-fertilizer
plantas.meaning: A potted plant with a fertilizer badge. Used for plant care and the feeding schedule.
plantas.drawing: A potted plant with a fertilizer badge. Used for plant care and the feeding schedule.
plantas.why: The plant-care family (plant-light, plant-water, plant-humidity) has no feeding need. fertilizer is the farm sack. names.mjs flags 'contains fertilizer', which is the family modifier.

producto.name: prototype-mobile
producto.meaning: Mobile prototype: a clickable prototype on a phone
producto.drawing: Mobile prototype: a clickable prototype on a phone
producto.why: wireframe and mockup have -mobile variants and prototype doesn't.

producto.name: prototype-hotspot
producto.meaning: Prototype hotspot: the clickable area that links one screen to the next
producto.drawing: Prototype hotspot: the clickable area that links one screen to the next
producto.why: prototype is the whole click-through. The hotspot is the area a designer draws on one frame.

producto.name: affinity-map
producto.meaning: Affinity map: research notes grouped into themes
producto.drawing: Affinity map: research notes grouped into themes
producto.why: empathy-map is the four-quadrant persona canvas. Affinity mapping is how teams make sense of research notes. Draw two clusters of notes, never a grid.

producto.name: release-check
producto.meaning: Shipped: a release that is out
producto.drawing: Shipped: a release that is out
producto.why: release-clock is a scheduled release, and no icon says a release has shipped. deploy-check (desarrollo) is about the pipeline.

producto.name: retrospective
producto.meaning: Retrospective: what went well and what to change, after a sprint
producto.drawing: Retrospective: what went well and what to change, after a sprint
producto.why: sprint-check closes the sprint. The retro is the meeting that follows it.

producto.name: layout-grid
producto.meaning: Layout grid: the columns laid over a frame
producto.drawing: Layout grid: the columns laid over a frame
producto.why: guides are single lines and pixel-grid is pixels. The column grid of every design tool and design system is missing.

producto.name: safe-area
producto.meaning: Safe area: the screen region clear of notches and system bars
producto.drawing: Safe area: the screen region clear of notches and system bars
producto.why: thumb-zone is where a thumb reaches. The safe area is where content can go.

producto.name: above-the-fold
producto.meaning: Above the fold: what a page shows before any scrolling
producto.drawing: Above the fold: what a page shows before any scrolling
producto.why: heatmap-scroll measures how far people scroll. The fold line is the layout idea.

producto.name: sprint-play
producto.meaning: Start sprint: begin a planned sprint
producto.drawing: Start sprint: begin a planned sprint
producto.why: sprint and sprint-check exist. Starting a sprint is the other action every tracker has.

producto.name: feature-flag-person
producto.meaning: Targeted flag: a feature turned on for chosen people or segments
producto.drawing: Targeted flag: a feature turned on for chosen people or segments
producto.why: rollout releases to a percentage of users. Targeting turns the feature on for named users or segments.

redes.name: topology-star
redes.meaning: A central node with six nodes around it, each linked only to the center: star topology, hub and spoke.
redes.drawing: A central node with six nodes around it, each linked only to the center: star topology, hub and spoke.
redes.why: The topology family (ring, bus, mesh, tree) shares one node and lacks the star, which the scope names. datos' network is a hub with three spokes, the generic node graph, and topology-ring's ring of six makes the two easy to tell apart. If the main session prefers, star-topology keywords on network say it instead. Lucide's graph-hub (fan-out) maps here too.

redes.name: globe-x
redes.meaning: The globe with an x badge, used when a website is down or unreachable, or there's no internet.
redes.drawing: The globe with an x badge, used when a website is down or unreachable, or there's no internet.
redes.why: globe-alert is a domain issue (misconfigured DNS, expired certificate). The down state sits beside it the way server-x sits beside server-alert.

restaurante.name: drive-through
restaurante.meaning: A car in profile at a service window under an awning: drive-thru ordering, a pickup mode in fast-food apps
restaurante.drawing: A car in profile at a service window under an awning: drive-thru ordering, a pickup mode in fast-food apps
restaurante.why: Those two draw the food. The scope names drive-throughs as a place and an ordering mode, and nothing draws the lane. The car is in profile, the view DESIGN.md allows.

restaurante.name: pizza-box
restaurante.meaning: An open pizza box with the lid raised over the pizza: pizza delivery and takeaway, pizzerias
restaurante.drawing: An open pizza box with the lid raised over the pizza: pizza delivery and takeaway, pizzerias
restaurante.why: takeout-box is the folded noodle pail. The pizza box is flat and square, drawn open so the pizza tells it (a closed one would read as any box). 'Contains box' is its plain name, like lunch-box.

restaurante.name: bread-basket
restaurante.meaning: A small woven basket with rolls and a baguette: bread service at the table
restaurante.drawing: A small woven basket with rolls and a baguette: bread service at the table
restaurante.why: The picnic basket is a lidded hamper and bread is a loaf on its own. The bread basket is the open table basket with bread standing in it, like egg-basket in fiestas.

restaurante.name: map-pin-utensils
restaurante.meaning: A map pin with a fork and knife: a restaurant's location, restaurants on the map, places to eat nearby
restaurante.drawing: A map pin with a fork and knife: a restaurant's location, restaurants on the map, places to eat nearby
restaurante.why: utensils is the restaurant and place-setting-search is the act of searching. The pin marks where a restaurant is, as map-pin-paw and map-pin-medical do for their categories. map-pin is the family's base.

restaurante.name: takeout-bag-clock
restaurante.meaning: A takeout bag with a clock: a scheduled order, order ahead, pickup time
restaurante.drawing: A takeout bag with a clock: a scheduled order, order ahead, pickup time
restaurante.why: The food counterpart of takeaway-cup-clock in bebidas (Order ahead), in the takeout-bag family. bag-clock is a retail pre-order on the shopping bag, not a food order scheduled for later.

restaurante.name: reservation-x
restaurante.meaning: A reservation with an x badge: a cancelled booking or a no-show
restaurante.drawing: A reservation with an x badge: a cancelled booking or a no-show
restaurante.why: Completes the reservation states (check, clock, plus) with the x the set uses for cancelled (plane-x, calendar-x, train-x). The desk-x search hit is rrhh's desk.

restaurante.name: map-pin-coffee
restaurante.meaning: A map pin with a coffee cup inside: cafés on a map (the Coffee filter in maps, store finders in coffee-chain apps).
restaurante.drawing: A map pin with a coffee cup inside: cafés on a map (the Coffee filter in maps, store finders in coffee-chain apps).
restaurante.why: map-pin-utensils (approved) marks restaurants. Cafés are their own map category. It is a map-pin family member, not a badge, so restaurante's 21% badge share is unchanged.

ropa.name: suspenders
ropa.meaning: Two straps with clips at their ends: suspenders, braces
ropa.drawing: Two straps with clips at their ends: suspenders, braces
ropa.why: It is a different accessory. The search hits are dispositivos' Spanish 'suspender' (sleep mode).

ropa.name: boot-knee-high
ropa.meaning: A tall boot up to the knee: knee-high boot
ropa.drawing: A tall boot up to the knee: knee-high boot
ropa.why: boot is the ankle boot. This is a kind, with the shaft up to the knee, named base-first like sneaker-high-top.

ropa.name: fabric-windproof
ropa.meaning: The fabric swatch with wind lines bouncing off it: windproof, wind-resistant
ropa.drawing: The fabric swatch with wind lines bouncing off it: windproof, wind-resistant
ropa.why: It belongs to the fabric-property family (waterproof, breathable, stretch, sun protection). Wind is not covered.

ropa.name: fabric-thermal
ropa.meaning: The fabric swatch with warmth rising from it: thermal, insulated, keeps you warm
ropa.drawing: The fabric swatch with warmth rising from it: thermal, insulated, keeps you warm
ropa.why: Breathable keeps you cool. Thermal keeps you warm, a common property in outdoor retail.

rrhh.name: candidate-x
rrhh.meaning: Reject candidate: the candidate résumé with an x badge
rrhh.drawing: Reject candidate: the candidate résumé with an x badge
rrhh.why: screening is the stage; rejecting is the action applicant-tracking tools put on each candidate

rrhh.name: candidate-star
rrhh.meaning: Shortlisted candidate: the candidate résumé with a star badge
rrhh.drawing: Shortlisted candidate: the candidate résumé with a star badge
rrhh.why: talent-pool is the group kept for later; the star marks a shortlisted candidate inside an open pipeline

rrhh.name: job-offer-check
rrhh.meaning: Offer accepted: the job offer (hand holding the briefcase) with a check badge
rrhh.drawing: Offer accepted: the job offer (hand holding the briefcase) with a check badge
rrhh.why: briefcase-check is the position filled, from the employer's side; this is the candidate's answer to the offer

rrhh.name: job-offer-x
rrhh.meaning: Offer declined: the job offer with an x badge
rrhh.drawing: Offer declined: the job offer with an x badge
rrhh.why: briefcase-x is the position closed; this is the candidate declining

rrhh.name: overtime
rrhh.meaning: Overtime: a clock whose filled sector runs past the hour, with a plus, for paid hours beyond the schedule
rrhh.drawing: Overtime: a clock whose filled sector runs past the hour, with a plus, for paid hours beyond the schedule
rrhh.why: hourly-rate is the pay per hour and clock-plus adds time to a timer; overtime is a payroll item and an attendance status of its own

rrhh.name: flexible-hours
rrhh.meaning: Flexible hours: a clock with a two-headed arrow around its face, flextime
rrhh.drawing: Flexible hours: a clock with a two-headed arrow around its face, flextime
rrhh.why: hybrid-work is where people work; flexible hours is when they choose to. work-life-balance is a seesaw with a briefcase and a heart.

rrhh.name: meal-voucher
rrhh.meaning: Meal voucher: a voucher card with a fork and knife, a food benefit (vales de despensa, ticket restaurant)
rrhh.drawing: Meal voucher: a voucher card with a fork and knife, a food benefit (vales de despensa, ticket restaurant)
rrhh.why: benefits is the bundle and coupon is a retail discount; the meal voucher is the most common single benefit in Latin America and Europe

salud.name: iv-bag
salud.meaning: The IV bag alone with its line: infusion, saline, IV therapy, vitamin drip
salud.drawing: The IV bag alone with its line: infusion, saline, IV therapy, vitamin drip
salud.why: iv-drip hangs the bag on a pole with a drip chamber. The migration note calls the bag alone related but not the same. The 'bag' contains is only the word.

salud.name: pulse-oximeter
salud.meaning: Finger clip with a reading: pulse oximeter, blood oxygen, SpO2
salud.drawing: Finger clip with a reading: pulse oximeter, blood oxygen, SpO2
salud.why: No finger clip or blood-oxygen icon exists, and health apps use one widely.

salud.name: neck-brace
salud.meaning: Head in profile wearing a cervical collar: neck injury, whiplash
salud.drawing: Head in profile wearing a cervical collar: neck injury, whiplash
salud.why: Like arm-sling and leg-cast, it is the injury device. It sits on anatomia's head-side, because the bare neck didn't read in round 7. 'braces' (datos) is a different word.

salud.name: eye-patch
salud.meaning: An eye patch on its strap: eye injury, amblyopia treatment
salud.drawing: An eye patch on its strap: eye injury, amblyopia treatment
salud.why: Eye care has the chart, drops and lenses but no patch. sistema's 'patch' is the adhesive bandage, so the contains is only the word.

salud.name: contact-lens-case
salud.meaning: Two-cup lens case with its screw lids: contact lens care
salud.drawing: Two-cup lens case with its screw lids: contact lens care
salud.why: contact-lens is the lens alone. The case is used for care and reorders. Its family base is contact-lens.

salud.name: tooth-extraction
salud.meaning: Molar lifted out of the gum line with an arrow up: extraction, oral surgery
salud.drawing: Molar lifted out of the gum line with an arrow up: extraction, oral surgery
salud.why: Broken is an injury. Extraction is a core dental procedure, next to filling and implant, and is missing.

salud.name: insulin-pump
salud.meaning: Small pump with its tube and infusion set: insulin pump, diabetes therapy
salud.drawing: Small pump with its tube and infusion set: insulin pump, diabetes therapy
salud.why: The pen is an injection. The pump is worn therapy with tubing. industria's 'pump' is only the word.

salud.name: helicopter-medical
salud.meaning: Helicopter in profile with the medical cross: air ambulance, medevac
salud.drawing: Helicopter in profile with the medical cross: air ambulance, medevac
salud.why: ambulance is the road vehicle. This is aviacion's helicopter in profile with the cross, following salud's -medical family (house-medical, phone-medical).

salud.name: heart-scan
salud.meaning: Heart inside scan corners: heart-rate check with the camera, health scan
salud.drawing: Heart inside scan corners: heart-rate check with the camera, health scan
salud.why: heart-pulse is the rhythm line. The scan family (face-scan, food-scan, leaf-scan) explains the name.

salud.name: head-side-cough
salud.meaning: Head in profile coughing out a spray of drops: cough, cold, contagion
salud.drawing: Head in profile coughing out a spray of drops: cough, cold, contagion
salud.why: head-side is the body region. The spray makes it the symptom. medicine-bottle only tags cough.

salud.name: headache
salud.meaning: Head in profile with pain strokes at the temple: headache, migraine
salud.drawing: Head in profile with pain strokes at the temple: headache, migraine
salud.why: head-side is tagged headache as a region. As toothache sits next to tooth, the pain strokes make it the symptom. Drop it if the tag is enough.

salud.name: hand-medical
salud.meaning: Open hand holding the medical cross: medical aid, health coverage, patient care
salud.drawing: Open hand holding the medical cross: medical aid, health coverage, patient care
salud.why: healthcare is a heart with a cross. The palm holding the cross is aid or coverage, as donation holds the heart. It is in the -medical family.

salud.name: sharps-container
salud.meaning: Lidded bin with a syringe going in: sharps disposal, needle bin
salud.drawing: Lidded bin with a syringe going in: sharps disposal, needle bin
salud.why: biohazard is the hazard sign. The needle bin is the clinic object for disposal.

salud.name: lab-results-check
salud.meaning: Lab results with a check badge: results within normal range, or reviewed and signed off by the doctor, in a patient portal (MyChart, Quest, LabCorp).
salud.drawing: Lab results with a check badge: results within normal range, or reviewed and signed off by the doctor, in a patient portal (MyChart, Quest, LabCorp).
salud.why: lab-results-alert is an abnormal result, lab-results-clock is results pending, and lab-results is the report itself. A patient portal also needs the 'normal / reviewed' state that pairs with the alert. The family already uses clock and alert, so check follows its logic.

salud.name: prescription-x
salud.meaning: A prescription with an x badge: refill request denied by the doctor, or the prescription cancelled, in a pharmacy app's order status.
salud.drawing: A prescription with an x badge: refill request denied by the doctor, or the prescription cancelled, in a pharmacy app's order status.
salud.why: prescription-check is ready for pickup and prescription-clock is in progress. Pharmacy apps (CVS, Walgreens) also show denied or cancelled. pill-x is a missed dose, a different object (the pill) and a different state (adherence).

salud.name: insurance-health-check
salud.meaning: Health insurance with a check badge: coverage verified, in network, eligibility confirmed (provider directories, clinic check-in, insurer apps).
salud.drawing: Health insurance with a check badge: coverage verified, in network, eligibility confirmed (provider directories, clinic check-in, insurer apps).
salud.why: insurance-health is the plan itself. Booking and directory apps (Zocdoc's in-network badge, clinic intake 'insurance verified') need the verified state on it, and Gota's verified is a generic seal. names.mjs reports 'contains health-check (sistema)', the healthy-service status. That is a word overlap only: the name follows the family's rule (base insurance-health plus the badge), as salud's other badges do. Salud's badges go from 18 to 21 of about 128 (16 %), under one in five.

seguridad-laboral.name: ear-protection
seguridad-laboral.meaning: Hard-shell ear defenders on their headband: hearing protection, noise area
seguridad-laboral.drawing: Hard-shell ear defenders on their headband: hearing protection, noise area
seguridad-laboral.why: earmuffs (ropa) are fluffy winter ear warmers and earplugs (bienestar) are for sleep. The scope names ear protection, the PPE item (ISO 7010 M003). The silhouettes are close, so the judge may decide.

seguridad-laboral.name: respirator
seguridad-laboral.meaning: A half-face respirator with its two filter cartridges: respiratory protection, dust, fumes
seguridad-laboral.drawing: A half-face respirator with its two filter cartridges: respiratory protection, dust, fumes
seguridad-laboral.why: gas-mask is the full-face mask with one canister. The half-face respirator with two cartridges is the everyday PPE the scope names (ISO 7010 M017).

seguridad-laboral.name: safety-harness
seguridad-laboral.meaning: A full-body safety harness with its lanyard and hook: fall protection, work at height
seguridad-laboral.drawing: A full-body safety harness with its lanyard and hook: fall protection, work at height
seguridad-laboral.why: harness (mascotas) is a dog's walking harness. The scope names the fall-arrest harness (ISO 7010 M018).

seguridad-laboral.name: laser-hazard
seguridad-laboral.meaning: The laser warning symbol, a burst with its beam line: laser radiation hazard
seguridad-laboral.drawing: The laser warning symbol, a burst with its beam line: laser radiation hazard
seguridad-laboral.why: The scope names the laser hazard sign (ISO 7010 W004), and nothing draws it. SF's laser.burst is the same burst.

seguridad-laboral.name: falling-objects
seguridad-laboral.meaning: A block falling toward a hard hat: falling objects hazard, overhead work
seguridad-laboral.drawing: A block falling toward a hard hat: falling objects hazard, overhead work
seguridad-laboral.why: suspended-load is a load hanging from a hook. The scope names falling objects (ISO 7010 W035).

seguridad-laboral.name: hot-surface
seguridad-laboral.meaning: Heat waves rising off a flat surface: hot surface warning, burn hazard
seguridad-laboral.drawing: Heat waves rising off a flat surface: hot surface warning, burn hazard
seguridad-laboral.why: heat-transfer (ciencia) is physics, and face-hot and heat-level are about people and cooking. Hot surface (ISO 7010 W017) is a standard hazard sign with no icon.

seguridad-laboral.name: environmental-hazard
seguridad-laboral.meaning: The GHS environment pictogram, a bare tree and a dead fish: hazardous to the aquatic environment
seguridad-laboral.drawing: The GHS environment pictogram, a bare tree and a dead fish: hazardous to the aquatic environment
seguridad-laboral.why: Completes the GHS set: flammable, oxidizer, explosive, corrosive, toxic and health hazard are drawn, but GHS09 isn't. It has two small subjects that don't overlap, so the critics should check it at 18 px.

seguridad-laboral.name: emergency-stop
seguridad-laboral.meaning: The mushroom-head emergency stop button on its box: e-stop, kill switch
seguridad-laboral.drawing: The mushroom-head emergency stop button on its box: e-stop, kill switch
seguridad-laboral.why: The scope names the emergency stop, and none is drawn. Draw it in profile on its box so it isn't read as a target from above.

seguridad-laboral.name: eyewash
seguridad-laboral.meaning: A head in profile with two water jets rising to the eye: eyewash station
seguridad-laboral.drawing: A head in profile with two water jets rising to the eye: eyewash station
seguridad-laboral.why: emergency-shower is the deluge shower, though its keywords mention eyewash. The scope names the eyewash as its own item, and ISO 7010 has its own sign for it (E011).

seguridad-laboral.name: fire-blanket
seguridad-laboral.meaning: A fire blanket pulled from its wall pouch by its two tabs: kitchen and lab fire safety
seguridad-laboral.drawing: A fire blanket pulled from its wall pouch by its two tabs: kitchen and lab fire safety
seguridad-laboral.why: The only item on the scope's fire-safety list that isn't drawn.

seguridad-laboral.name: hazmat-suit
seguridad-laboral.meaning: A hooded hazmat suit with its wide visor: hazardous materials, decontamination
seguridad-laboral.drawing: A hooded hazmat suit with its wide visor: hazardous materials, decontamination
seguridad-laboral.why: coveralls (ropa) are work overalls, and spacesuit has a helmet and backpack. The hooded suit with a wide visor is for hazmat response. Check it against the spacesuit.

seguridad-laboral.name: fire-alarm-bell
seguridad-laboral.meaning: The electric gong bell on the wall with its striker: fire alarm bell, evacuation alarm
seguridad-laboral.drawing: The electric gong bell on the wall with its striker: fire alarm bell, evacuation alarm
seguridad-laboral.why: fire-alarm is the pull station, school-bell is a hand bell, and bell-ringing is the notification bell. Lucide's bell-electric (the gong) has no equivalent. The name joins the fire-alarm family.

seguridad-laboral.name: hard-hat-x
seguridad-laboral.meaning: Hard hat with an x badge: PPE missing, not compliant
seguridad-laboral.drawing: Hard hat with an x badge: PPE missing, not compliant
seguridad-laboral.why: hard-hat-check means PPE compliant. Missing PPE is the violation that site apps and PPE-detection cameras flag.

seguridad-laboral.name: fire-extinguisher-check
seguridad-laboral.meaning: Fire extinguisher with a check badge: extinguisher inspected
seguridad-laboral.drawing: Fire extinguisher with a check badge: extinguisher inspected
seguridad-laboral.why: fire-extinguisher-clock means inspection due. Inspected is the state that resolves it.

seguridad-laboral.name: work-permit-check
seguridad-laboral.meaning: Permit to work with a check badge: permit approved
seguridad-laboral.drawing: Permit to work with a check badge: permit approved
seguridad-laboral.why: work-permit is the permit itself. Approved is the state that permit-to-work systems turn on.

seguridad-laboral.name: clipboard-alert
seguridad-laboral.meaning: Clipboard with an alert badge: incident report, safety observation
seguridad-laboral.drawing: Clipboard with an alert badge: incident report, safety observation
seguridad-laboral.why: clipboard-x (archivos) is a rejected task and flag-report is a generic report. Incident reporting is central to safety apps and has no icon. It is named into the clipboard family.

seguridad-laboral.name: chemical-spill
seguridad-laboral.meaning: A tipped flask with its puddle spreading: chemical spill, spill response
seguridad-laboral.drawing: A tipped flask with its puddle spreading: chemical spill, spill response
seguridad-laboral.why: spill (limpieza) is a knocked-over drink and toxic-waste is a drum. A lab or industrial chemical spill (spill kits, incident type) is shown by its flask.

seguridad-laboral.name: work-permit-clock
seguridad-laboral.meaning: Permit to work with a clock badge. Used for a permit pending approval or close to its time limit in permit-to-work software.
seguridad-laboral.drawing: Permit to work with a clock badge. Used for a permit pending approval or close to its time limit in permit-to-work software.
seguridad-laboral.why: The check is the approved permit. Permit-to-work systems list permits waiting for approval, and permits running out on their time limit, as their own status. The permit is a document people manage. The 'contains clock' conflict is just the badge family. The category's badges stay near 11%.

senales.name: stairwell
senales.meaning: A door with stairs on it: stairwell access, the stairs as the way out
senales.drawing: A door with stairs on it: stairwell access, the stairs as the way out
senales.why: stairs-up and stairs-down point a direction and stairs (hogar) is the object. The stairwell door is the wayfinding sign for stair access, and emergency-exit (seguridad-laboral) is the running figure.

simbolos.name: ampersand-double
simbolos.meaning: Double ampersand (&&): the AND operator of code
simbolos.drawing: Double ampersand (&&): the AND operator of code
simbolos.why: ampersand is one glyph. && is the operator people look for in code docs.

simbolos.name: asterism
simbolos.meaning: Asterism (⁂): three asterisks in a triangle, the typographic section break
simbolos.drawing: Asterism (⁂): three asterisks in a triangle, the typographic section break
simbolos.why: asterisk is a single sign and the asterism is a sign of its own. Keep each asterisk to three strokes so it holds at 18 px.

simbolos.name: interrobang
simbolos.meaning: Interrobang (‽): a question and an exclamation in one sign
simbolos.drawing: Interrobang (‽): a question and an exclamation in one sign
simbolos.why: question-mark and exclamation-mark exist separately. The combined mark is a single typographic character.

simbolos.name: x-bar
simbolos.meaning: X-bar (x̄): the sample mean in statistics
simbolos.drawing: X-bar (x̄): the sample mean in statistics
simbolos.why: letter-x is the bare letter. The overline turns it into the mean, the statistics sign people use most after sigma.

simbolos.name: omega
simbolos.meaning: Omega (Ω): ohms and resistance, and the last of a series
simbolos.drawing: Omega (Ω): ohms and resistance, and the last of a series
simbolos.why: pi and lambda are the only Greek letters drawn so far. Omega is the unit sign of resistance.

simbolos.name: phi
simbolos.meaning: Phi (φ): the golden ratio and magnetic flux
simbolos.drawing: Phi (φ): the golden ratio and magnetic flux
simbolos.why: golden-ratio (formas) is the spiral and phi is the letter. Draw it open, not as a circle with a slash, so it stays apart from empty-set and diameter.

simbolos.name: mu
simbolos.meaning: Mu (µ): the micro prefix and a population mean
simbolos.drawing: Mu (µ): the micro prefix and a population mean
simbolos.why: There is no micro sign. micro-sd-card and microphone are objects.

simbolos.name: sigma
simbolos.meaning: Lowercase sigma (σ): the standard deviation
simbolos.drawing: Lowercase sigma (σ): the standard deviation
simbolos.why: sum is the capital Σ of summation. Lowercase σ is the standard deviation found in every statistics tool.

simbolos.name: per-ten-thousand
simbolos.meaning: Per ten thousand (‱): basis points
simbolos.drawing: Per ten thousand (‱): basis points
simbolos.why: per-mille (‰) is per thousand. Basis points are the unit finance uses.

simbolos.name: gender-male
simbolos.meaning: Male sign (♂): the male option in a form or a filter
simbolos.drawing: Male sign (♂): the male option in a form or a filter
simbolos.why: The set has no gender signs. The restroom figures in senales show people, not the signs.

simbolos.name: gender-female
simbolos.meaning: Female sign (♀): the female option in a form or a filter
simbolos.drawing: Female sign (♀): the female option in a form or a filter
simbolos.why: The set has no gender signs.

simbolos.name: gender-transgender
simbolos.meaning: Transgender sign (⚧): the transgender option in a form
simbolos.drawing: Transgender sign (⚧): the transgender option in a form
simbolos.why: The closest icon is gender-male, proposed in this list. This is the third sign of the gender set that forms offer.

simbolos.name: gender-nonbinary
simbolos.meaning: Non-binary sign (⚲): the non-binary option in a form
simbolos.drawing: Non-binary sign (⚲): the non-binary option in a form
simbolos.why: The closest icon is gender-male, proposed in this list. This sign completes the gender set.

simbolos.name: currency-taka
simbolos.meaning: Taka sign (৳): the currency of Bangladesh
simbolos.drawing: Taka sign (৳): the currency of Bangladesh
simbolos.why: currency-rupee (comercio) is India's sign, and the taka isn't drawn.

simbolos.name: currency-dram
simbolos.meaning: Dram sign (֏): the currency of Armenia
simbolos.drawing: Dram sign (֏): the currency of Armenia
simbolos.why: The dram sign isn't drawn.

simbolos.name: currency-lari
simbolos.meaning: Lari sign (₾): the currency of Georgia
simbolos.drawing: Lari sign (₾): the currency of Georgia
simbolos.why: The lari sign isn't drawn.

simbolos.name: currency-riyal
simbolos.meaning: Saudi riyal sign: the currency of Saudi Arabia (its 2025 sign)
simbolos.drawing: Saudi riyal sign: the currency of Saudi Arabia (its 2025 sign)
simbolos.why: currency-dirham is the UAE's new sign. The Saudi riyal got a sign of its own.

simbolos.name: currency-cedi
simbolos.meaning: Cedi sign (₵): the currency of Ghana
simbolos.drawing: Cedi sign (₵): the currency of Ghana
simbolos.why: cent (¢) is a small c with a slash, and the cedi is a capital C crossed by a vertical stroke. Keep the C at full height so the two signs don't look the same.

simbolos.name: letter-c-cedilla
simbolos.meaning: Letter Ç: the C with a cedilla used in French, Portuguese, Catalan, and Turkish
simbolos.drawing: Letter Ç: the C with a cedilla used in French, Portuguese, Catalan, and Turkish
simbolos.why: letter-n-tilde already adds a Latin letter beyond A–Z, and Ç is the next most used. Its cedilla hangs below the letter, so it doesn't blur at 18 px the way umlaut dots do.

simbolos.name: not-element-of
simbolos.meaning: The element-of sign crossed by a short stroke: 'is not an element of' (∉), for math and equation editors.
simbolos.drawing: The element-of sign crossed by a short stroke: 'is not an element of' (∉), for math and equation editors.
simbolos.why: Its own Unicode relation, drawn with a short typographic stroke the way not-equal is drawn next to equals, not the engine's full-icon slash. It completes the set signs simbolos already has (element-of, subset, superset, empty-set). The 'contains element-of' conflict is the family logic of not-equal. This is the weakest of the list: keep it only if simbolos wants its set signs complete.

simbolos.name: not-subset
simbolos.meaning: The subset sign crossed by a short stroke: 'is not a subset of' (⊄), for math and equation editors.
simbolos.drawing: The subset sign crossed by a short stroke: 'is not a subset of' (⊄), for math and equation editors.
simbolos.why: Same reasoning as not-element-of: a separate sign with a short stroke, like not-equal. The 'contains subset' conflict is the family logic. Weak, so drop it together with not-element-of if the set signs shouldn't grow.

social.name: post-carousel
social.meaning: Carousel post: several photos swiped through in one post
social.drawing: Carousel post: several photos swiped through in one post
social.why: post is a single item, and view-carousel (navegacion) is a layout, not a post.

social.name: story-highlight
social.meaning: Story highlight: saved stories pinned to a profile
social.drawing: Story highlight: saved stories pinned to a profile
social.why: story-ring is an unseen story, and highlights (foto-video) are video clips.

social.name: friend-suggestions
social.meaning: People you may know: suggested accounts to follow
social.drawing: People you may know: suggested accounts to follow
social.why: profile-card is one profile, and the list of suggestions is a feature of its own.

social.name: member-requests
social.meaning: Join requests: approve or decline people asking to join a group
social.drawing: Join requests: approve or decline people asking to join a group
social.why: people-plus is joining a group. This is the admin's queue of requests.

social.name: person-alert
social.meaning: Flagged account: a user reported or under review
social.drawing: Flagged account: a user reported or under review
social.why: flag-report (sistema) reports content. This marks the account itself, next to person-mute and person-block.

social.name: post-hide
social.meaning: Hide post: show less of this in the feed
social.drawing: Hide post: show less of this in the feed
social.why: person-mute hides a whole account. This hides one post.

social.name: post-embed
social.meaning: Embed post: put a post on another site
social.drawing: Embed post: put a post on another site
social.why: post-quote reposts with a comment. Embedding places the post on another page.

social.name: people-globe
social.meaning: Public group: a group anyone can find and join
social.drawing: Public group: a group anyone can find and join
social.why: people-lock is a private group, and the public group is its pair.

social.name: review-reply
social.meaning: Reply to review: the owner answers a review
social.drawing: Reply to review: the owner answers a review
social.why: review-edit writes a review. The reply is the business's answer under it.

soporte.name: ticket-x
soporte.meaning: Closed ticket: the ticket with an x badge, closed without a fix, canceled or spam; also a canceled event ticket
soporte.drawing: Closed ticket: the ticket with an x badge, closed without a fix, canceled or spam; also a canceled event ticket
soporte.why: ticket-check is solved; the support ticket family has no closed or canceled state

soporte.name: ticket-search
soporte.meaning: Find ticket: the ticket with the magnifier badge, searching the queue
soporte.drawing: Find ticket: the ticket with the magnifier badge, searching the queue
soporte.why: search-question searches help articles, not tickets

soporte.name: sla-check
soporte.meaning: SLA met: the SLA shield and clock with a check badge
soporte.drawing: SLA met: the SLA shield and clock with a check badge
soporte.why: help desks report met and breached SLAs side by side; only the breach exists

soporte.name: status-page-alert
soporte.meaning: Active incident: the status page with an alert badge
soporte.drawing: Active incident: the status page with an alert badge
soporte.why: server-alert is one machine. This is the public status page announcing an incident. Scheduled maintenance is already wrench-clock, so no status-page-clock.

soporte.name: smartphone-repair-clock
soporte.meaning: Repair in progress: the phone repair with a clock badge
soporte.drawing: Repair in progress: the phone repair with a clock badge
soporte.why: 'repair complete' exists but the step before it doesn't (scope: repairs and their status). smartphone-clock is screen time, another family.

soporte.name: smartphone-water-damage
soporte.meaning: Liquid damage: a phone with a drop, for repair intake
soporte.drawing: Liquid damage: a phone with a drop, for repair intake
soporte.why: after the cracked screen, liquid damage is the most common repair; hogar's water-damage is a house

soporte.name: laptop-repair
soporte.meaning: Laptop repair: a laptop with the wrench, as on smartphone-repair
soporte.drawing: Laptop repair: a laptop with the wrench, as on smartphone-repair
soporte.why: the same service for the other device repair shops take in; the laptop family (lock, check) has no repair

soporte.name: appliance-repair
soporte.meaning: Appliance repair: a washing machine with the wrench, home appliance service
soporte.drawing: Appliance repair: a washing machine with the wrench, home appliance service
soporte.why: car-repair and smartphone-repair exist; appliance service (washers, fridges) is the third big repair trade

soporte.name: complaint-book
soporte.meaning: Complaints book: the official register where customers file a complaint (libro de reclamaciones, livro de reclamações, hojas de reclamaciones)
soporte.drawing: Complaints book: the official register where customers file a complaint (libro de reclamaciones, livro de reclamações, hojas de reclamaciones)
soporte.why: complaint is one complaint in a bubble. The complaints book is a legally required register that shops in Peru, Portugal and Spain must link on their sites.

soporte.name: field-service
soporte.meaning: Field service: a van in profile with the wrench, on-site service and repair visits
soporte.drawing: Field service: a van in profile with the wrench, on-site service and repair visits
soporte.why: technician-clock is the arrival window of one person; field service is the service fleet sent on site, in field-service tools

soporte.name: ticket-minus
soporte.meaning: A ticket with a minus; remove a ticket from an order.
soporte.drawing: A ticket with a minus; remove a ticket from an order.
soporte.why: Taking one ticket off an order is a real checkout action, the opposite of ticket-plus.

transito.name: trolleybus
transito.meaning: A bus with two trolley poles up to the overhead wires: trolleybus lines
transito.drawing: A bus with two trolley poles up to the overhead wires: trolleybus lines
transito.why: The poles to the wires make it a kind of its own among buses by kind. tram runs on rails.

transito.name: bus-articulated
transito.meaning: A long articulated bus with its accordion joint: bus rapid transit and high-capacity lines
transito.drawing: A long articulated bus with its accordion joint: bus rapid transit and high-capacity lines
transito.why: Buses by kind have city, coach, double-decker, school, mini, and electric, but not the articulated BRT bus. Risk: keep it long but in proportion so it doesn't read as a train car.

transito.name: bus-x
transito.meaning: A bus with an x badge: cancelled bus service
transito.drawing: A bus with an x badge: cancelled bus service
transito.why: train-x exists and bus-alert is a disruption or detour, not a cancellation. This completes the pair.

transito.name: transit-card-sync
transito.meaning: A transit card with a sync badge: auto top-up, autoload.
transito.drawing: A transit card with a sync badge: auto top-up, autoload.
transito.why: transit-card-plus is a one-time top-up. The sync badge is the automatic reload that a transit card's app sets up.

vehiculos.name: backhoe-loader
vehiculos.meaning: A backhoe loader in profile, with a front bucket and a rear digging arm: site work and equipment rental
vehiculos.drawing: A backhoe loader in profile, with a front bucket and a rear digging arm: site work and equipment rental
vehiculos.why: excavator has only the arm and runs on tracks; wheel-loader has only the front bucket. A wheeled machine with both is its own kind. 'contains loader' is the loading spinner in sistema, which is unrelated.

vehiculos.name: motor-grader
vehiculos.meaning: A motor grader in profile, a long frame with the blade under its middle: road building and grading
vehiculos.drawing: A motor grader in profile, a long frame with the blade under its middle: road building and grading
vehiculos.why: The set has no grader. The roller compacts and the grader levels, and the long frame with a blade under its middle is unlike any other machine.

vehiculos.name: telehandler
vehiculos.meaning: A telehandler in profile, a telescopic boom with forks: lifting loads on a building site
vehiculos.drawing: A telehandler in profile, a telescopic boom with forks: lifting loads on a building site
vehiculos.why: boom-lift carries a basket for people, and forklift (logistica) has a vertical mast. A telehandler is an angled telescopic boom that ends in forks.

vehiculos.name: concrete-pump-truck
vehiculos.meaning: A truck with a folded concrete boom on its back: concrete pumping and pours
vehiculos.drawing: A truck with a folded concrete boom on its back: concrete pumping and pours
vehiculos.why: cement-mixer carries a drum and crane-truck carries a knuckle crane. A boom folded along the truck is what shows the pump.

vehiculos.name: asphalt-paver
vehiculos.meaning: An asphalt paver in profile, with the hopper in front and the screed behind: road paving
vehiculos.drawing: An asphalt paver in profile, with the hopper in front and the screed behind: road paving
vehiculos.why: The roller compacts and the paver lays the asphalt; road crews need both. Risk: keep it to a clear profile (hopper, canopy, screed) so it doesn't read as boxes.

vehiculos.name: site-dumper
vehiculos.meaning: A small site dumper with its skip in front of the driver: moving material around a building site
vehiculos.drawing: A small site dumper with its skip in front of the driver: moving material around a building site
vehiculos.why: dump-truck is a road truck with its bed behind the cab. A site dumper is a small open machine that tips forward.

vehiculos.name: logging-truck
vehiculos.meaning: A truck carrying long logs between stakes: timber hauling
vehiculos.drawing: A truck carrying long logs between stakes: timber hauling
vehiculos.why: flatbed-truck is empty. The logs held between upright stakes are what show a timber truck.

vehiculos.name: monster-truck
vehiculos.meaning: A pickup body on giant wheels: monster truck shows and off-road fun
vehiculos.drawing: A pickup body on giant wheels: monster truck shows and off-road fun
vehiculos.why: The oversized wheels make it a show vehicle, not a pickup or car-offroad.

vehiculos.name: dune-buggy
vehiculos.meaning: An open buggy with a roll cage and big tires: dune and off-road rides
vehiculos.drawing: An open buggy with a roll cage and big tires: dune and off-road rides
vehiculos.why: car-offroad is a closed 4x4 and quad-bike is ridden astride. A buggy is an open frame under a roll cage.

vehiculos.name: auto-rickshaw
vehiculos.meaning: A three-wheeled auto rickshaw (tuk-tuk) in profile: taxis and tours in the cities that use them
vehiculos.drawing: A three-wheeled auto rickshaw (tuk-tuk) in profile: taxis and tours in the cities that use them
vehiculos.why: The set has no three-wheeled motor taxi; tricycle is pedalled and moped has no cabin. Material has electric_rickshaw. Keywords: tuk-tuk.

vehiculos.name: pedicab
vehiculos.meaning: A cycle rickshaw with a covered passenger seat: pedicab rides and city tours
vehiculos.drawing: A cycle rickshaw with a covered passenger seat: pedicab rides and city tours
vehiculos.why: tricycle is a trike for its rider. A pedicab carries passengers in a hooded seat in front of or behind the cyclist.

vehiculos.name: motorcycle-sidecar
vehiculos.meaning: A motorcycle with a sidecar: sidecar rides and tours
vehiculos.drawing: A motorcycle with a sidecar: sidecar rides and tours
vehiculos.why: The sidecar is the kind. It follows the motorcycle-* family (sport, cruiser, dirt, electric).

vehiculos.name: penny-farthing
vehiculos.meaning: A penny-farthing with its huge front wheel: vintage cycling and heritage rides
vehiculos.drawing: A penny-farthing with its huge front wheel: vintage cycling and heritage rides
vehiculos.why: It doesn't share the bicycle base. The giant front wheel makes it a kind of its own and the universal sign for an old bicycle.

vehiculos.name: trailer-teardrop
vehiculos.meaning: A teardrop camper trailer: small towable campers
vehiculos.drawing: A teardrop camper trailer: small towable campers
vehiculos.why: caravan is a full box caravan and trailer-enclosed is a cargo box. The small rounded teardrop is the popular minimal camper. It is in the trailer-* family.

vehiculos.name: car-minus
vehiculos.meaning: A car with a minus badge: remove a vehicle from a garage, fleet, or account
vehiculos.drawing: A car with a minus badge: remove a vehicle from a garage, fleet, or account
vehiculos.why: car-plus adds a vehicle and nothing removes one. It is a badge sibling on the car base.

vehiculos.name: car-x
vehiculos.meaning: A car with an x badge: vehicle unavailable or booking cancelled
vehiculos.drawing: A car with an x badge: vehicle unavailable or booking cancelled
vehiculos.why: car-alert is a problem with the car, not a cancellation. This matches plane-x, train-x, and ship-x, which already exist.

vehiculos.name: car-heart
vehiculos.meaning: A car with a heart: saved or favorite vehicles in listings and rentals
vehiculos.drawing: A car with a heart: saved or favorite vehicles in listings and rentals
vehiculos.why: Vehicles have no favorite state. This matches hotel-heart.

vehiculos.name: car-gear
vehiculos.meaning: A car with a gear: vehicle settings and preferences in a car app
vehiculos.drawing: A car with a gear: vehicle settings and preferences in a car app
vehiculos.why: car-connected is telematics and car-repair (conduccion) is the mechanic. Nothing means the vehicle's settings. The gear is a standard glyph badge.

vehiculos.name: bicycle-lock
vehiculos.meaning: A bicycle with a padlock: bike locked, secured bike, the end of a bike-share ride
vehiculos.drawing: A bicycle with a padlock: bike locked, secured bike, the end of a bike-share ride
vehiculos.why: bike-rack (transito) is a parking place that has 'lock' as a keyword. This is the locked state on the bike itself, the bicycle's version of car-lock. A U-lock drawn alone would read as a magnet, so the padlock is a badge.

vehiculos.name: moped-electric
vehiculos.meaning: The moped with a bolt: an electric moped, as in e-moped sharing fleets.
vehiculos.drawing: The moped with a bolt: an electric moped, as in e-moped sharing fleets.
vehiculos.why: The family already draws its electric kinds (motorcycle-electric, bicycle-electric, car-electric, truck-electric). Shared e-mopeds are their own fleet in sharing apps.

ventanas.name: window-maximize
ventanas.meaning: Maximize window: the title-bar action that makes the window fill the screen
ventanas.drawing: Maximize window: the title-bar action that makes the window fill the screen
ventanas.why: minimize and close (window-x) exist but the third title-bar action doesn't. maximize (navegacion) is bare arrows, and window-controls shows all three buttons at once.

ventanas.name: window-restore
ventanas.meaning: Restore window: bring a maximized window back to its own size (two frames overlapped)
ventanas.drawing: Restore window: bring a maximized window back to its own size (two frames overlapped)
ventanas.why: fullscreen-exit leaves full screen. Restore undoes maximize, and it is the title-bar button between minimize and close.

ventanas.name: window-center
ventanas.meaning: Center window: place the window in the middle of the screen
ventanas.drawing: Center window: place the window in the middle of the screen
ventanas.why: The snaps tile a window to edges and corners. Centering is the other tiling command.

ventanas.name: window-snap-left-third
ventanas.meaning: Snap to left third: tile the window into the left third of the screen
ventanas.drawing: Snap to left third: tile the window into the left third of the screen
ventanas.why: The snaps split the screen in halves and quarters. Thirds are the other grid window tiling uses.

ventanas.name: window-snap-center-third
ventanas.meaning: Snap to center third: tile the window into the middle third of the screen
ventanas.drawing: Snap to center third: tile the window into the middle third of the screen
ventanas.why: The middle third has no half or quarter equivalent.

ventanas.name: window-snap-right-third
ventanas.meaning: Snap to right third: tile the window into the right third of the screen
ventanas.drawing: Snap to right third: tile the window into the right third of the screen
ventanas.why: Same reason as the left third.

ventanas.name: window-offline
ventanas.meaning: Offline state: the app can't reach the network
ventanas.drawing: Offline state: the app can't reach the network
ventanas.why: The scope lists offline among the app states and it isn't drawn. window-alert is a generic error, and wifi-off and cloud-off show the connection, not the app screen.

ventanas.name: window-clock
ventanas.meaning: Session expired: the app timed out and asks to sign in again
ventanas.drawing: Session expired: the app timed out and asks to sign in again
ventanas.why: hourglass-end is time running out anywhere. This is the app's own state, next to window-block and window-pause.

ventanas.name: window-update
ventanas.meaning: Update required: the app must update before it continues
ventanas.drawing: Update required: the app must update before it continues
ventanas.why: window-sync reloads, and update-dot (sistema) is a notice from the system. This is the app state that blocks use until the update.

ventanas.name: widgets-plus
ventanas.meaning: Add widget: put a new widget on the home screen or a dashboard
ventanas.drawing: Add widget: put a new widget on the home screen or a dashboard
ventanas.why: widgets is the set. Adding one is its own action, as apps-plus is for apps.

ventanas.name: apps-minus
ventanas.meaning: Remove app: uninstall an app or take it off the launcher
ventanas.drawing: Remove app: uninstall an app or take it off the launcher
ventanas.why: apps-plus adds an app and no icon removes one.

ventanas.name: wallpaper
ventanas.meaning: Wallpaper: the picture behind the desktop or the home screen
ventanas.drawing: Wallpaper: the picture behind the desktop or the home screen
ventanas.why: lock-screen is the locked phone, and wallpaper-roll (hogar) is decorating paper. The screen background is a setting of its own.

ventanas.name: start-menu
ventanas.meaning: Start menu: the app menu that rises from the taskbar
ventanas.drawing: Start menu: the app menu that rises from the taskbar
ventanas.why: taskbar is the bar itself, and the launcher menu that opens from it isn't drawn. menu-bar is the top bar.

ventanas.name: toolbar-floating
ventanas.meaning: Floating toolbar: a toolbar that floats over the canvas or a selection
ventanas.drawing: Floating toolbar: a toolbar that floats over the canvas or a selection
ventanas.why: toolbar is docked along the top of the window. A floating bar (on design canvases or as a text-selection menu) sits over the content.

ventanas.name: dock-hide
ventanas.meaning: Hide dock: keep the dock or taskbar out of sight until the pointer reaches it
ventanas.drawing: Hide dock: keep the dock or taskbar out of sight until the pointer reaches it
ventanas.why: dock is the bar itself, and auto-hide is a setting of it. window-minimize sends one window down.

viajes.name: luggage-open
viajes.meaning: An open suitcase: packing for a trip, what's in my bag
viajes.drawing: An open suitcase: packing for a trip, what's in my bag
viajes.why: luggage-check means bags packed (done). The open suitcase is packing in progress, a state of the same object. The car-trunk-open search hit is unrelated.

viajes.name: clock-tower
viajes.meaning: A generic clock tower: city landmarks and sights
viajes.drawing: A generic clock tower: city landmarks and sights
viajes.why: The scope asks for generic landmarks. monument is an obelisk and observation-tower is a TV tower. A clock tower belongs to no single real monument.

viajes.name: triumphal-arch
viajes.meaning: A generic triumphal arch monument: landmarks and sights
viajes.drawing: A generic triumphal arch monument: landmarks and sights
viajes.why: arch (construccion) is the structural arch and natural-arch is a rock. The arch monument is a type found in many cities, not one real monument.

viajes.name: hotel-x
viajes.meaning: A hotel with an x badge: booking cancelled or no availability
viajes.drawing: A hotel with an x badge: booking cancelled or no availability
viajes.why: hotel has check (booked), heart, and search but no cancellation. This matches plane-x.

viajes.name: luggage-alert
viajes.meaning: A suitcase with an alert: delayed or damaged baggage report
viajes.drawing: A suitcase with an alert: delayed or damaged baggage report
viajes.why: baggage-tag-search tracks a bag. Reporting a delayed or damaged bag is its own airline and travel-insurance flow.

viajes.name: map-pin-bed
viajes.meaning: A map pin with a bed inside: hotels and lodging on a map, the Hotels marker that every map app has.
viajes.drawing: A map pin with a bed inside: hotels and lodging on a map, the Hotels marker that every map app has.
viajes.why: hotel is the building, not a marker. The map-pin family already marks planes, buses, trains, tents and (approved) restaurants. It is a family member, not a badge, so it doesn't count toward viajes' badge share.

viajes.name: travel-visa-clock
viajes.meaning: A visa with a clock badge: a visa or travel authorization in process, waiting for a decision (eVisa or ETA status trackers).
viajes.drawing: A visa with a clock badge: a visa or travel authorization in process, waiting for a decision (eVisa or ETA status trackers).
viajes.why: travel-visa-check means approved and travel-visa-x means refused. The pending state between them is what a visa tracker shows most of the time. passport-clock is a different document, expiring.
